161.official_section_title: Special provisions as to compensation in case of hit and run motor accident
161.official_text: (1) The Central Government shall, by notification in the Official Gazette, make a scheme for the administration of a fund, to be known as the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund, which shall be used for providing compensation to the victims of hit and run motor accidents... (3) The amount of compensation shall be: (a) in respect of the death of any person resulting from a hit and run motor accident, a fixed sum of two lakh rupees; (b) in respect of grievous hurt to any person resulting from a hit and run motor accident, a fixed sum of fifty thousand rupees.
161.simplified_explanation: Provides statutory compensation to victims of hit-and-run accidents where the offending vehicle cannot be identified: Rs. 2,00,000 in case of death, and Rs. 50,000 for grievous hurt, payable from the Central Motor Vehicle Accident / Solatium Fund.
161.applicability_notes: Statutory relief for victims or families when the offending driver flees unidentified.

166.official_section_title: Application for compensation before Claims Tribunal (MACT)
166.official_text: (1) An application for compensation arising out of an accident of the nature specified in sub-section (1) of section 165 may be made— (a) by the person who has sustained the injury; or (b) by the owner of the property; or (c) where death has resulted from the accident, by all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased... (3) No application for compensation shall be entertained unless it is made within six months of the occurrence of the accident.
166.simplified_explanation: Victims of motor accidents or their legal heirs can file an application for just compensation before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT). Must be filed within 6 months of the accident.
166.applicability_notes: Primary forum for claiming comprehensive third-party insurance compensation, medical reimbursements, and loss of future earnings following vehicle collisions.

139_cmvr.official_section_title: Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989 Rule 139 - Production of electronic documents
139_cmvr.official_text: The driver or conductor of a motor vehicle shall produce certificate of registration, insurance, fitness, permit, driving licence and pollution under control certificate in physical or electronic form on demand by any police officer in uniform or any other officer authorised... The documents produced in electronic form through DigiLocker or mParivahan platform shall be deemed to be valid under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
139_cmvr.simplified_explanation: Rule 139 legally mandates that digital driving licences, RC books, insurance certificates, and PUCs displayed via DigiLocker or mParivahan have the exact same legal validity as physical documents. Traffic police cannot insist on physical originals or issue fines if digital documents are presented.
139_cmvr.applicability_notes: Statutory shield against traffic police harassment for not carrying physical laminated licences or RC smart cards.
139_cmvr.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

100_cmvr.official_section_title: Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989 Rule 100 - Safety glass and visual transmission
100_cmvr.official_text: The glass of the windscreen and rear window of every motor vehicle shall be made of safety glass and shall have a visual transmission of light not less than 70 per cent. The glasses of side windows of every motor vehicle shall have a visual transmission of light not less than 50 per cent.
100_cmvr.simplified_explanation: Prescribes visual light transmission (VLT) standards: front and rear windscreens must maintain at least 70% VLT, and side windows at least 50% VLT. Challans cannot be legally issued if safety film or tinted glass conforms to these statutory light transmission standards.
100_cmvr.applicability_notes: Defense against wrongful traffic challans for car window tint conforming to 70%/50% statutory transparency limits.
100_cmvr.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

50_cmvr.official_section_title: Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989 Rule 50 - High Security Registration Plates (HSRP)
50_cmvr.official_text: The registration mark shall be displayed on a High Security Registration Plate (HSRP) conforming to the specifications prescribed by the Central Government, including chromium-based hologram, non-removable snap lock, and unique laser branded identification number.
50_cmvr.simplified_explanation: Mandates HSRP plates with tamper-proof snap locks and holograms. Motorists who have applied and possess valid booking receipts during notified state grace periods cannot be fined for non-affixation.
50_cmvr.applicability_notes: Governs HSRP number plate enforcement, booking grace periods, and invalid challan challenges.

113.official_text: (1) The State Government may prescribe conditions for the issue of permits for transport vehicles by the State or Regional Transport Authorities and may prohibit or restrict the use of such vehicles in any area or on any route. (2) Except as may be prescribed, no person shall drive or cause or allow to be driven in any public place any motor vehicle or trailer— (a) the unladen weight of which exceeds the unladen weight specified in the certificate of registration; or (b) the laden weight of which exceeds the gross vehicle weight specified in the certificate of registration.

136A.official_section_title: Electronic monitoring and enforcement of road safety
136A.official_text: (1) The State Government shall ensure electronic monitoring and enforcement of road safety in the manner provided under sub-section (2) on national highways, state highways, roads or in any urban city within a State which has a population up to such limits as may be prescribed by the Central Government. (2) The Central Government shall make rules for the electronic monitoring and enforcement of road safety including speed cameras, closed-circuit television cameras, speed guns, body wearable cameras and such other technology. Explanation.--For the purpose of this section the expression 'body wearable camera' means a mobile audio and video capture device worn on the body or uniform of a person authorised by the State Government.
136A.simplified_explanation: Provides the statutory framework for electronic traffic policing, automated speed cameras, CCTV red-light detection, ANPR cameras, and mandatory traffic police body-worn cameras.
136A.applicability_notes: Central provision for contesting erroneous automated e-challans, speed trap inaccuracies, and demanding body camera footage during traffic stops.

199A.official_text: (1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a juvenile, the guardian of such juvenile or the owner of the motor vehicle shall be deemed to be guilty of the contravention and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly... (2) In addition to the penalty under sub-section (1), such guardian or owner shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with a fine of twenty-five thousand rupees. (4) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a juvenile, the registration of the motor vehicle used in the commission of the offence shall be cancelled for a period of twelve months. (5) ...such juvenile shall not be eligible to be granted a driving licence... until such juvenile has attained the age of twenty-five years.
199A.simplified_explanation: Holds vehicle owners or parents directly criminally responsible if a minor drives their vehicle, punishable by up to 3 years imprisonment and a twenty-five thousand rupee fine, along with 1-year vehicle registration cancellation and barring the juvenile from obtaining a driving licence until age 25.
199A.applicability_notes: Directly applies to underage driving enforcement, parental liability for minor-driven vehicles, and vehicle impoundment cases.

128.official_section_title: Safety measures for drivers and pillion riders
128.official_text: (1) No driver of a two-wheeled motor vehicle shall carry more than one person in addition to himself on the motorcycle and no such person shall be carried otherwise than sitting on a proper seat securely fixed to the motorcycle behind the driver's seat with appropriate safety measures. (2) In addition to the safety measures mentioned in sub-section (1), the Central Government may, prescribe other safety measures for the drivers and pillion riders of two-wheeled motor vehicles.
128.simplified_explanation: Prohibits triple riding on two-wheelers, mandating that motorcycle drivers may carry only one pillion passenger seated securely behind the driver with proper footrests and safety measures.
128.applicability_notes: Directly governs triple riding motorcycle enforcement, carrying multiple adults on two-wheelers, and vehicle instability penalties.

132.official_section_title: Duty of driver to stop in certain cases
132.official_text: (1) The driver of a motor vehicle shall cause the vehicle to stop and remain stationary so long as may reasonably be necessary— (a) when required to do so by any police officer not below the rank of a Sub-Inspector in uniform, or in Gujarat by any police officer in uniform authorised in this behalf, or (b) when required to do so by any person in charge of an animal if such person apprehends that the animal is or will be frightened by the vehicle... (2) The driver of a motor vehicle shall, on demand by a person giving reasonable ground to believe that the driver has been involved in an accident with that person... give his name and address...
132.simplified_explanation: Imposes a mandatory legal duty on every vehicle driver to halt and remain stationary when signaled to stop by an authorized police officer in uniform or following a road accident.

179.official_section_title: Disobedience of orders, obstruction and refusal of information
179.official_text: (1) Whoever wilfully disobeys any direction lawfully given by any person or authority empowered under this Act to give such direction, or obstructs any person or authority in the discharge of any functions which such person or authority is required or empowered under this Act to discharge, shall, if no other penalty is provided for the offence be punishable with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees. (2) Whoever, being required by or under this Act to supply any information, wilfully withholds such information or gives information which he knows to be false or which he does not believe to be true, shall, if no other penalty is provided for the offence, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.
179.simplified_explanation: Imposes a fine up to two thousand rupees for willfully disobeying lawful directions of traffic authorities, obstructing officers in their duty, or withholding required information or supplying false details.

110A.official_text: (1) The Central Government may, by order, direct a manufacturer to recall motor vehicles of a particular type or its variant, if— (a) a defect in that particular type of motor vehicle, or a component of that motor vehicle, may cause harm to the environment or to the driver or occupants of such motor vehicle or to other road users; or (b) a defect in that particular type of motor vehicle has been reported to the Central Government by— (i) such percentage of owners... (2) Where the manufacturer... undertakes to recall... the manufacturer shall— (a) reimburse the buyers... or (b) replace the defective motor vehicle with another motor vehicle of similar or better specifications.
110A.simplified_explanation: Empowers the Central Government to order mandatory vehicle recalls for critical manufacturing, brake, or steering defects, legally obligating automobile manufacturers to either give buyers a 100% full refund or replace the vehicle with a brand new one.
legal_ingredients: Systemic defect in vehicle type or component causing safety or environmental hazard
Mandatory order of recall or voluntary recall by manufacturer
Statutory obligation to reimburse full price or replace defective vehicle
110A.punishment_or_remedy: Full vehicle replacement or 100% financial reimbursement to buyer; fine up to Rs 1 Crore on non-compliant manufacturer under Section 182A.
exceptions_and_limitations: Defect must be a manufacturing or design defect, not damage caused by post-purchase accidents or unauthorized third-party modifications.
110A.amendment_status: In force; inserted by Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019.
110A.jurisdiction: Central (Ministry of Road Transport and Highways - MoRTH).
110A.applicability_notes: Statutory lemon law protection for Indian motor vehicle and EV owners against dangerous manufacturing faults.

115.official_section_title: Power to restrict the use of vehicles
115.official_text: The State Government or any authority authorised in this behalf by the State Government, if satisfied that it is necessary in the interest of public safety or convenience, or because of the nature of any road or bridge, may, by notification in the Official Gazette, prohibit or restrict, subject to such exceptions and conditions as may be specified in the notification, the driving of motor vehicles or of any specified class or description of motor vehicles or the use of trailers either generally in a specified area or on a specified road.
115.simplified_explanation: Authorizes State Governments and traffic commissioners to restrict certain classes of vehicles (e.g. heavy goods trucks in city limits during peak hours) on specific roads or bridges for public safety.
legal_ingredients: Gazette notification by State Government or authorized traffic authority
Restriction justified by public safety, convenience, or road/bridge condition
115.punishment_or_remedy: Violation punishable under Section 177 / 179; however, un-notified or arbitrary curbs can be challenged in High Court.
exceptions_and_limitations: Emergency vehicles (ambulances, fire engines) are universally exempt.
115.applicability_notes: Legal basis for peak-hour heavy vehicle bans, pedestrian zones, and one-way traffic restrictions.

133.official_section_title: Duty of owner of motor vehicle to give information
133.official_text: The owner of a motor vehicle the driver or conductor of which is accused of any offence under this Act shall, on the demand of any police officer authorised in this behalf by the State Government, give all information regarding the name and address of, and the licence held by, the driver or conductor which is in his possession or could by reasonable diligence be ascertained by him.
133.simplified_explanation: Requires the registered owner of a motor vehicle to provide the true name, address, and driving licence details of the person who was driving the vehicle when an offence or accident occurred.
legal_ingredients: Accusation of motor vehicle offence involving vehicle
Demand by authorized police officer
Owner obligation to disclose driver identity and licence details
133.punishment_or_remedy: Failure by owner punishable under Section 187 with fine up to Rs 500 or imprisonment up to 3 months.
exceptions_and_limitations: Owner is not liable if vehicle was stolen and theft was promptly reported to police.
133.applicability_notes: Prevents vehicle owners from hiding reckless drivers, hit-and-run perpetrators, or unauthorized minors.

147.official_section_title: Requirements of policies and limits of liability
147.official_text: (1) In order to comply with the requirements of this Chapter, a policy of insurance must be a policy which— (a) is issued by a person who is an authorised insurer; and (b) insures the person or classes of persons specified in the policy to the extent specified in sub-section (2)— (i) against any liability which may be incurred by him in respect of the death of or bodily injury to any person, including owner of the goods or his authorised representative carried in the motor vehicle or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the motor vehicle in a public place.
147.simplified_explanation: Mandates compulsory Third Party Insurance coverage for every motor vehicle in India, guaranteeing compensation for death, bodily injury, or third-party property damage arising from road accidents.
legal_ingredients: Policy issued by IRDAI-authorized insurer
Compulsory coverage for third-party death, bodily injury, and property damage
Motor vehicle used in public place
147.punishment_or_remedy: Driving without third-party insurance punishable under Section 196 (fine up to Rs 2,000 / Rs 4,000 or imprisonment up to 3 months).
exceptions_and_limitations: Policy does not cover contractual liability unless specifically endorsed.
147.amendment_status: In force; Chapter XI substituted by Act 32 of 2019.
147.jurisdiction: Central (Applies across all motor vehicles in India).
147.applicability_notes: Statutory bedrock of road accident compensation and Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT) litigation.

149.official_section_title: Duty of insurers to satisfy judgments and awards against persons insured
149.official_text: (1) If, after a certificate of insurance has been issued... judgment or award in respect of any such liability as is required to be covered by a policy... is obtained against any person insured by the policy, then... the insurer shall, subject to the provisions of this section, pay to the person entitled to the benefit of the decree any sum not exceeding the sum assured payable thereunder.
149.simplified_explanation: Imposes an absolute statutory duty on insurance companies to pay accident compensation awards decreed by the MACT Court directly to the victim or their family, preventing insurers from evading payments.
legal_ingredients: Valid certificate of insurance issued
MACT judgment or court decree obtained against insured driver/owner
Statutory obligation on insurer to satisfy award amount
149.punishment_or_remedy: Direct execution and recovery of award from insurer assets.
exceptions_and_limitations: Insurer can defend only on limited statutory grounds (fake driving licence, unauthorized vehicle use) under Section 149(2), and even then must 'pay and recover'.
149.amendment_status: In force; 'pay and recover' principle affirmed by Supreme Court.
149.applicability_notes: Protects road accident victims from driver insolvency; insurer must pay victim first and recover from owner later.

164.official_section_title: Payment of compensation in case of death or grievous hurt
164.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be. (2) In any claim for compensation under sub-section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt... was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle.
164.simplified_explanation: Provides guaranteed, fast no-fault compensation: Rs 5 Lakh for death and Rs 2.5 Lakh for grievous injury, without the victim needing to prove whose fault or negligence caused the accident.
legal_ingredients: Death or grievous hurt arising out of motor vehicle accident
Claimant NOT required to plead or prove wrongful act, negligence, or fault
Fixed statutory compensation: Rs 5,00,000 for death, Rs 2,50,000 for grievous hurt
164.punishment_or_remedy: Immediate no-fault statutory compensation of Rs 5 Lakh (death) or Rs 2.5 Lakh (grievous hurt) paid by owner/insurer within 30 days.
exceptions_and_limitations: If claimant receives Section 164 compensation, they cannot pursue a fault-based claim under Section 166.
164.amendment_status: In force; inserted by 2019 Amendment Act replacing former Section 163A.
164.applicability_notes: Lifesaver for poor accident victims; eliminates lengthy multi-year negligence trials.

182.official_text: (1) Whoever, being disqualified under this Act for holding or obtaining a driving licence, drives a motor vehicle in a public place or applies for or obtains a driving licence or, not being entitled to have a driving licence issued to him free of endorsement, applies for or obtains a driving licence without giving particulars of such endorsement shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine to the extent of ten thousand rupees, or with both.
182.simplified_explanation: Imposes criminal punishment—fine up to Rs 10,000, imprisonment up to 3 months, or both—on anyone who drives a vehicle or secretly applies for a new driving licence while disqualified or suspended by RTO/Court.
legal_ingredients: Person disqualified or licence suspended under MV Act
Driving motor vehicle in public place or applying for new licence while disqualified
182.punishment_or_remedy: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both; revocation of newly obtained fraudulent licence.
exceptions_and_limitations: Does not apply if disqualification order was formally stayed by appellate transport authority or court.
182.amendment_status: In force; fine increased from Rs 500 to Rs 10,000 by 2019 Amendment Act.
182.applicability_notes: Severely punishes suspended drunk drivers or disqualified road offenders who continue driving illegally.

186.official_section_title: Driving when mentally or physically unfit to drive
186.official_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle in any public place when he is to his knowledge suffering from any disease or disability calculated to cause his driving of the vehicle to be a source of danger to the public, shall be punishable for the first offence with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees and for a second or subsequent offence with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees.
186.simplified_explanation: Penalizes driving a motor vehicle in public when suffering from a severe physical or mental condition (e.g. epileptic seizures, uncorrected vision loss, acute impairment) that endangers road safety.
legal_ingredients: Driving motor vehicle in a public place
Knowledge of suffering from disease or disability calculated to cause danger to public
186.punishment_or_remedy: Fine up to Rs 1,000 for first offence, Rs 2,000 for subsequent offence; suspension of driving licence under Section 19.
exceptions_and_limitations: Persons driving specially adapted invalid carriages or vehicles modified for persons with disabilities with RTO medical clearance are exempt.
186.amendment_status: In force; fines updated by Act 32 of 2019.
186.applicability_notes: Statutory ground for revoking driving licences of individuals who develop incapacitating medical conditions.

197.official_text: (1) Whoever takes and drives away any motor vehicle without having either the consent of the owner thereof or other lawful authority shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both... (2) Any person who, knowing that a motor vehicle has been so taken, drives it or allows himself to be carried in it without such consent or authority shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
197.simplified_explanation: Penalizes joyriding or taking away someone's motor vehicle without owner consent (even without intent to permanently steal it) with imprisonment up to 3 months, fine up to Rs 5,000, or both, covering both driver and passengers.
legal_ingredients: Taking and driving away motor vehicle without owner consent or lawful authority
Or traveling as passenger knowing vehicle was taken without consent
197.punishment_or_remedy: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both.
exceptions_and_limitations: Accused had reasonable belief that he had lawful authority or that owner would have consented under circumstances.
197.amendment_status: In force; fine raised from Rs 500 to Rs 5,000 by 2019 Amendment Act.
197.applicability_notes: Applies to unauthorized joyriding, mechanics taking customer cars for unauthorized personal trips, or valet misuse.

198.official_text: Whoever otherwise than with lawful authority or reasonable excuse enters or mounts any stationary motor vehicle or tampers with the brake or any part of the mechanism of a motor vehicle shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
198.simplified_explanation: Makes it an offence to enter, mount, or tamper with the brakes or mechanical parts of a stationary motor vehicle without lawful authority or reasonable excuse, punishable with fine up to Rs 1,000.
legal_ingredients: Stationary motor vehicle
Entering, mounting, or tampering with brakes or mechanism without lawful authority or reasonable excuse
198.punishment_or_remedy: Fine up to one thousand rupees.
exceptions_and_limitations: Authorized police officers executing lawful seizure or towing with reasonable excuse.
198.amendment_status: In force; fine raised from Rs 100 to Rs 1,000 by 2019 Amendment Act.
198.applicability_notes: Protects private parked vehicles from vandalism, unauthorized entry, or private recovery agents tampering with brakes.

201.official_section_title: Penalty for causing obstruction to free flow of traffic
201.official_text: (1) Whoever keeps a disabled vehicle on any public place, in such a manner, so as to cause impediment to the free flow of traffic, shall be liable for penalty up to fifty rupees per hour, so long as it remains situated... (2) Where any vehicle is abandoned or left unattended in a public place for more than ten hours by its owner or driver or is parked in a place where parking is legally prohibited, its removal by a towing service or its immobilisation by the use of wheel clamps may be authorised by a police officer in uniform... Provided that the owner of the motor vehicle shall be liable to pay the towing charges and the penalty as prescribed.
201.simplified_explanation: Governs traffic obstruction, vehicle breakdown, and towing: police may authorize towing or wheel clamping only for vehicles parked illegally or left unattended for over 10 hours, with prescribed statutory towing fees.
legal_ingredients: Disabled vehicle left causing impediment to traffic flow
Or vehicle left unattended for over 10 hours or in strictly prohibited no-parking zone
Authorization by police officer in uniform for towing or wheel clamping
201.punishment_or_remedy: Prescribed statutory towing fee and obstruction penalty; illegal private towing charges can be refunded.
exceptions_and_limitations: Towing is unlawful if driver or occupant is seated inside vehicle, or if breakdown warning lights were displayed and driver was arranging repair.
201.amendment_status: In force; towing rules updated by 2019 Amendment Act.
201.applicability_notes: Essential statutory check against arbitrary private towing contractors and exorbitant towing fines.

209.official_text: No person prosecuted for an offence punishable under section 183 or section 184 shall be convicted unless— (a) he was warned at the time the offence was committed that the question of prosecuting him would be taken into consideration, or (b) within fourteen days from the commission of the offence, a notice specifying the nature of the alleged offence and the time and place where it is alleged to have been committed was served on or sent by registered post to him or the person registered as the owner of the vehicle.
209.simplified_explanation: Provides a powerful statutory protection for drivers: no person can be legally convicted or fined for speeding (Section 183) or dangerous driving (Section 184) unless warned at the time of the offence or served with a formal notice within 14 days.
legal_ingredients: Prosecution for speeding (S. 183) or dangerous driving (S. 184)
Statutory requirement: driver was warned at the spot, OR formal notice served/dispatched within 14 days
Failure of police to notify within 14 days completely bars lawful conviction
209.punishment_or_remedy: Absolute statutory bar on conviction; delayed traffic challans served months later are legally void.
exceptions_and_limitations: Bar does not apply if delay was caused by driver failing to provide correct registered address on Vahan portal.
209.jurisdiction: Central (Applies to all traffic courts across India).
209.applicability_notes: Key legal defense against delayed automated camera challans sent months after the alleged incident.

210B.official_section_title: Penalty for offence committed by an authority for enforcing this Act
210B.official_text: Any authority that is empowered to enforce the provisions of this Act shall, if such authority commits an offence under this Act, be liable for twice the penalty corresponding to that offence under this Act.
210B.simplified_explanation: Mandates that if a traffic police officer, transport inspector, or enforcement official commits a traffic violation (e.g. driving without helmet, jumping signal, using mobile while driving), they must pay TWICE (double) the normal fine.
legal_ingredients: Individual is an authority empowered to enforce the Motor Vehicles Act (traffic police, RTO officer)
Commission of traffic violation or offence under MV Act
Statutory mandate: double (2x) the penalty prescribed for ordinary citizens
210B.punishment_or_remedy: Twice (200%) the standard statutory penalty, plus departmental disciplinary inquiry.
exceptions_and_limitations: Police officers acting under bona fide emergency dispatch (pursuit of fleeing criminal) are protected.
210B.amendment_status: In force; landmark accountability provision inserted by Act 32 of 2019.
210B.applicability_notes: Crucial provision for citizen dignity; ensures traffic police are held to higher statutory standards than the public.

3.official_section_title: Prohibition of discrimination on ground of sex
3.official_text: (1) There shall be no discrimination among employees on the ground of sex in matters relating to wages by the same employer, in respect of the same work or work of a similar nature done by any employee. (2) No employer shall,— (i) for the purposes of complying with the provisions of sub-section (1), reduce the rate of wages of any employee; and (ii) make any discrimination on the ground of sex against employees in recruitment for the same work or work of similar nature...
3.simplified_explanation: Strictly prohibits wage discrimination on the ground of sex or gender for the same work or work of a similar nature.
3.applicability_notes: Directly applies where female workers or employees are paid lower wages or salaries than male colleagues doing the same work.
3.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
3.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

6.official_text: (1) Subject to the provisions of section 9, the appropriate Government shall fix the minimum rates of wages payable to employees in accordance with the provisions of section 8. (2) For the purpose of sub-section (1), the appropriate Government shall fix a minimum rate of wages— (a) for time work; or (b) for piece work...
6.simplified_explanation: Mandates that the appropriate government fix statutory minimum wage rates that employers are legally obligated to pay without exception.
6.applicability_notes: Governs situations where workers or employees are paid less than the legally mandated minimum floor wage or state minimum wage rates.
6.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
6.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

14.official_text: Where an employee whose minimum rate of wages has been fixed under this Code by the day, or by such other period as may be prescribed, works on any day in excess of the number of hours constituting a normal working day, the employer shall pay him for every hour or for part of an hour so worked in excess, at the overtime rate which shall not be less than twice the normal rate of wages.
14.simplified_explanation: Requires employers to pay overtime wages at not less than twice the normal wage rate for any hours worked beyond normal working hours.
14.applicability_notes: Direct statutory remedy when an employer forces employees to work extended hours, weekends, or shifts without mandatory double-rate overtime pay.
14.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
14.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

17.official_section_title: Time limit for payment of wages
17.official_text: (1) The employer shall pay or cause to be paid wages to the employees, engaged on— (a) daily basis, at the end of the shift; (b) weekly basis, on the last working day of the week, that is to say, before the weekly holiday; (c) fortnightly basis, before the end of the second day after the end of the fortnight; (d) monthly basis, before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month. (2) Where an employee has been— (i) removed, or dismissed from service; or (ii) retrenched or has resigned from service, or became unemployed due to closure of the establishment, the wages payable to him shall be paid within two working days of his removal, dismissal, retrenchment or, as the case may be, his resignation.
17.simplified_explanation: Strictly mandates wage payment deadlines (e.g. before the 7th of every month) and requires full and final wage settlement within two working days of resignation, removal, or termination.
17.applicability_notes: Primary section for delayed salary payments and for employers withholding full and final settlement (F&F) after an employee resigns or is terminated.
17.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
17.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

18.official_section_title: Deductions which may be made from wages
18.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, there shall be no deductions from the wages of the employee, except those authorised under this Code. (2) Deductions from the wages of an employee shall be made only in accordance with the provisions of this Code, and may be made only for the following purposes, namely:— (a) fines; (b) deductions for absence from duty; (c) deductions for damage to or loss of goods expressly entrusted to the employee...
18.simplified_explanation: Prohibits all unauthorized deductions from salary. Deductions can only be made for legally specified reasons (such as statutory PF/tax, proven absent days, or authorized recovery) subject to legal ceilings.
18.applicability_notes: Protects employees against arbitrary salary cuts, unilateral notice-period penalty deductions, unverified performance penalties, or failure to deposit PF.
18.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
18.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

45.official_section_title: Claims under Code and procedure thereof
45.official_text: (1) The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint one or more authorities, not below the rank of a Gazetted Officer, to hear and determine the claims which arises under the provisions of this Code. (2) The authority appointed under sub-section (1), while deciding the claim under that sub-section, may order, having regard to the circumstances under which the claim arises, the payment of compensation in addition to the claim determined, which may extend, in the case of minimum wages, to ten times of the amount of such claim...
45.simplified_explanation: Empowers designated Labour Authorities to hear worker wage claims and award compensation of up to ten times the unpaid or delayed amount in addition to the wages owed.
45.applicability_notes: The formal statutory dispute resolution route for recovery of unpaid wages, illegal deductions, and minimum wage shortfalls through Labour Commissioners and the Samadhan portal.
45.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
45.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

13.official_section_title: Number of hours of work which shall constitute a normal working day
13.official_text: (1) Where the minimum rates of wages have been fixed under this Code, the appropriate Government may— (a) fix the number of hours of work which shall constitute a normal working day inclusive of one or more specified intervals; (b) provide for a day of rest in every period of seven days which shall be allowed to all employees or to any specified class of employees and for the payment of remuneration in respect of such days of rest...
13.simplified_explanation: Mandates that normal working days cannot exceed statutory daily hour limits (8-9 hours) and legally guarantees a mandatory paid day of rest (weekly holiday) every seven days.
13.applicability_notes: Directly protects contract workers, security guards, and shift employees forced to work 7 days a week continuously without a mandatory weekly day off.
13.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
13.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

9.official_section_title: Power of Central Government to fix floor wage
9.official_text: (1) The Central Government may, after taking into account the minimum living standards of a worker, fix floor wage: Provided that different floor wages may be fixed for different geographical areas. (2) The minimum rates of wages fixed by the appropriate Government under section 6 shall not be less than the floor wage and if the minimum rates of wages fixed by the appropriate Government in respect of any employment are less than the floor wage, they shall not be reduced by the appropriate Government.
9.simplified_explanation: Empowers the Central Government to establish a statutory national floor wage below which no state or employer is legally permitted to pay any employee.
9.applicability_notes: Protects outsourced data processors, remote gig workers, and low-wage workers against predatory employer wage fixing below national baseline levels.
9.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
9.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

26.official_text: (1) There shall be paid to every employee, drawing wages not exceeding such amount per mensem as may be determined by notification, by the appropriate Government, by his employer, who has worked for not less than thirty days in an accounting year, an annual minimum bonus calculated at the rate of eight and one-third per cent of the wages earned by the employee or one hundred rupees, whichever is higher, whether or not the employer has any allocable surplus in the accounting year...
26.simplified_explanation: Mandates that every employee who has worked at least thirty days in an accounting year is legally entitled to an annual minimum bonus of 8.33% of wages.
26.applicability_notes: Statutory guarantee for employees whose employers arbitrarily withhold annual bonus payments claiming zero company profits.
keywords: eight and one third per cent
26.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
26.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

50.official_text: (1) Every employer of an establishment to which this Code applies shall maintain a register containing the details of the persons employed, muster roll, wages and such other details in such manner as may be prescribed. (2) Every employer shall display a notice on the notice board... (3) Every employer shall issue wage slips to the employees in such form and manner as may be prescribed.
50.simplified_explanation: Obligates employers to maintain statutory employment records, muster rolls, and to issue written wage slips specifying salary components and deductions to all workers.
50.applicability_notes: Direct basis for action against establishments that pay cash without payslips or conceal wage deductions and overtime hours.
50.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
50.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

51.official_section_title: Appointment of Inspector-cum-Facilitators and their powers
51.official_text: (1) The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint Inspector-cum-Facilitators for the purposes of this Code... (3) Every Inspector-cum-Facilitator shall be deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code... (4) The Inspector-cum-Facilitator may— (a) advise employers and workers relating to compliance with the provisions of this Code; (b) inspect the establishment as assigned to him; (c) examine any person found in any premises...
51.simplified_explanation: Authorizes statutory labour Inspector-cum-Facilitators to inspect workplaces, examine employer wage records, and investigate non-compliance with wage laws.
51.applicability_notes: Provides the statutory mechanism for workers to demand formal government labour inspections when companies refuse to rectify wage theft.
51.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
51.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

10.official_section_title: Wages of employee who works for less than normal working day
10.official_text: If an employee whose minimum rate of wages has been fixed by the day, works on any day on which he was employed for a number of hours less than the number which constitutes a normal working day, he shall, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, be entitled to receive wages in respect of work done on that day, as if he had worked for a full normal working day: Provided that he shall not be entitled to receive wages for a full normal working day— (i) in any case where his failure to work is caused by his unwillingness to work and not by the omission of the employer to provide him with work; and (ii) in such other cases and circumstances as may be prescribed.
10.simplified_explanation: Mandates that when a worker reports for duty but is given work for less than a normal working day due to employer's failure or lack of work, they must still be paid full normal daily wages.
10.applicability_notes: Protects daily wage and monthly employees from unpaid bench periods, factory machine breakdowns, or employer-induced downtime where the worker was present and willing to work.
10.citation: Code on Wages, 2019 (Act No. 29 of 2019), s. 10
10.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
10.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

15.official_text: All wages shall be paid in current coin or currency notes or by cheque or by crediting the wages in the bank account of the employee or by the electronic mode: Provided that the appropriate Government may, by notification, specify the industrial or other establishment, the employer of which shall pay to every person employed in such industrial or other establishment, the wages only by cheque or by crediting the wages in his bank account.
15.simplified_explanation: Requires all wages to be paid strictly in legal tender currency, by cheque, through direct bank account transfer, or via recognized electronic banking modes.
15.applicability_notes: Prevents off-the-books cash skimming or barter payments, and mandates verifiable banking records for wage disbursements across commercial establishments.
15.citation: Code on Wages, 2019 (Act No. 29 of 2019), s. 15
15.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
15.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

21.official_text: (1) A deduction under clause (c) or clause (n) of sub-section (2) of section 18 for damage to or loss of goods expressly entrusted to the employed person for custody, or for loss of money for which he is required to account, shall not exceed the amount of the damage or loss caused to the employer by the neglect or default of the employee. (2) A deduction shall not be made under sub-section (1) until the employee has been given an opportunity of showing cause against the deduction, or otherwise than in accordance with such procedure as may be prescribed.
21.simplified_explanation: Restricts wage deductions for damaged company goods or lost cash only to the actual loss caused by employee neglect, and strictly prohibits any deduction without first giving the employee a formal show-cause opportunity.
21.applicability_notes: Critical in employment exit settlements where employers arbitrarily deduct money for office laptop cosmetic wear, lost inventory, or damaged equipment without notice.
21.citation: Code on Wages, 2019 (Act No. 29 of 2019), s. 21
21.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
21.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

15.official_text: "Coercion" is the committing, or threatening to commit, any act forbidden by the Indian Penal Code, or the unlawful detaining, or threatening to detain, any property, to the prejudice of any person whatever, with the intention of causing any person to enter into an agreement.
15.simplified_explanation: Defines coercion as forcing someone to sign an agreement or settlement by unlawful detention of property or threats of unlawful acts.
15.applicability_notes: Applies when a citizen or vendor is forced to sign an unfair settlement, waiver, or release deed under threats or unlawful withholding of their assets.

19.official_section_title: Voidability of agreements without free consent
19.official_text: When consent to an agreement is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.
19.simplified_explanation: Gives the victim the legal right to cancel and invalidate any contract or agreement that they were tricked, coerced, or defrauded into signing.
19.applicability_notes: Enables citizens to rescind contracts entered into based on false misrepresentations or signed under financial duress.
19.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
19.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.

27.official_section_title: Agreement in restraint of trade, void
27.official_text: Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void.
27.simplified_explanation: Declares that any agreement or contract clause that restricts a person from practicing their lawful profession, trade, or business (such as post-employment non-compete clauses) is legally VOID and unenforceable in India.
27.applicability_notes: Key statutory defense for employees, consultants, and freelancers threatened with legal action under post-employment non-compete agreements.
27.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
27.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

37.official_text: The parties to a contract must either perform, or offer to perform, their respective promises, unless such performance is dispensed with or excused under the provisions of this Act, or of any other law.
37.simplified_explanation: Establishes the fundamental legal obligation that both parties who enter into an agreement must fulfill their agreed contractual promises.
37.applicability_notes: Foundation for any dispute where one party simply refuses to carry out agreed tasks, deliver goods, or return property as promised.
37.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

39.official_section_title: Effect of refusal of party to perform promise wholly
39.official_text: When a party to a contract has refused to perform, or disabled himself from performing, his promise in its entirety, the promisee may put an end to the contract, unless he has signified, by words or conduct, his acquiescence in its continuance.
39.simplified_explanation: Allows a party to terminate the contract when the other party completely refuses to perform or makes it impossible to fulfill their obligations.
39.applicability_notes: Applies when a contractor, vendor, or service provider abandons the project or announces they will not complete agreed work.
39.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

70.official_section_title: Obligation of person enjoying benefit of non-gratuitous act
70.official_text: Where a person lawfully does anything for another person, or delivers anything to him, not intending to do so gratuitously, and such other person enjoys the benefit thereof, the latter is bound to make compensation to the former in respect of, or to restore, the thing so done or delivered.
70.simplified_explanation: Mandates that when someone performs work or delivers services/goods for another person without intending it as free/charity, and the recipient enjoys the benefit, the recipient is legally bound to pay fair compensation.
70.applicability_notes: Crucial statutory provision for freelance professionals, designers, software developers, and small vendors whose delivered work was accepted and used but never paid for.
70.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
70.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

73.official_section_title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
73.official_text: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from the breach of it.
73.simplified_explanation: Entitles the aggrieved party to financial compensation and damages for direct monetary losses resulting from a breach of contract.
73.applicability_notes: Primary remedy for financial recovery in breach of contract cases, withheld security deposits, and contractor defaults.
73.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
73.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

74.official_section_title: Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for
74.official_text: When a contract has been broken, if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of such breach, or if the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused thereby, to receive from the party who has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or, as the case may be, the penalty stipulated for.
74.simplified_explanation: Prevents unfair or extortionate penalty clauses and unreasonable forfeiture of advance deposits, limiting compensation strictly to reasonable proven damages.
74.applicability_notes: Directly applies where vendors, sellers, or builders attempt to forfeit 100% of large advance deposits under harsh penalty clauses.
74.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
74.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

75.official_section_title: Party rightfully rescinding contract, entitled to compensation
75.official_text: A person who rightfully rescinds a contract is entitled to compensation for any damage which he has sustained through the non-fulfilment of the contract.
75.simplified_explanation: Clarifies that when an innocent party rightfully cancels an agreement due to the other party's breach or failure, they retain the legal right to claim compensation for all losses suffered.
75.applicability_notes: Directly supports claims where a citizen cancels a contract because the other party failed to deliver, and seeks reimbursement of advances and consequential losses.
75.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
75.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.

56.official_text: An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful.
56.simplified_explanation: Declares that a contract becomes void if unforeseen supervening events (natural disasters, severe medical emergencies, government prohibitions) make performance physically impossible (Doctrine of Frustration).
56.applicability_notes: Protects parties from penalty clauses and breach claims when events entirely beyond their control (pandemics, floods, sudden incapacitation) prevent fulfilling contractual dates.
56.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
56.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

65.official_section_title: Obligation of person who has received advantage under void agreement, or contract that becomes void
65.official_text: When an agreement is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under such agreement or contract is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it, to the person from whom he received it.
65.simplified_explanation: Mandates that when a contract is cancelled, frustrated, or becomes void, any person who took advance payments or benefits must refund or restore those benefits to the other party.
65.applicability_notes: Direct legal basis for compelling banquet halls, event organizers, or vendors to refund advance deposits when an event is cancelled due to impossibility or frustration.
65.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
65.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

18.official_text: "Misrepresentation" means and includes— (1) the positive assertion, in a manner not warranted by the information of the person making it, of that which is not true, though he believes it to be true; (2) any breach of duty which, without an intent to deceive, gains an advantage to the person committing it... by misleading another to his prejudice... (3) causing, however innocently, a party to an agreement, to make a mistake as to the substance of the thing which is the subject of the agreement.
18.simplified_explanation: Defines misrepresentation: making untrue assertions or misleading statements regarding the core subject of an agreement, even without deliberate criminal intent.
18.applicability_notes: Key statutory basis when an investor, buyer, or franchisee enters into an agreement based on false figures, fabricated profit claims, or misleading business representations.
18.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

16.official_text: (1) A contract is said to be induced by 'undue influence' where the relations subsisting between the parties are such that one of the parties is in a position to dominate the will of the other and uses that position to obtain an unfair advantage over the other. (2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing principle, a person is deemed to be in a position to dominate the will of another— (a) where he holds a real or apparent authority over the other, or where he stands in a fiduciary relation to the other; or (b) where he makes a contract with a person whose mental capacity is temporarily or permanently affected by reason of age, illness, or mental or bodily distress.
16.simplified_explanation: Defines undue influence where one party exploits a position of dominant authority, trust, or another's vulnerability (such as old age or distress) to extract an unfair contract.
16.applicability_notes: Ground for voiding unconscionable agreements signed by vulnerable senior citizens, dependent tenants, or distressed borrowers under dominant pressure.
16.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
16.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

17.official_text: 'Fraud' means and includes any of the following acts committed by a party to a contract, or with his connivance, or by his agent, with intent to deceive another party thereto or his agent, or to induce him to enter into the contract:— (1) the suggestion, as a fact, of that which is not true, by one who does not believe it to be true; (2) the active concealment of a fact by one having knowledge or belief of the fact; (3) a promise made without any intention of performing it; (4) any other act fitted to deceive; (5) any such act or omission as the law specially declares to be fraudulent.
17.simplified_explanation: Defines contractual fraud: active concealment of defects, deliberate falsehoods, or making promises with zero intention of fulfilling them to induce an agreement.
17.applicability_notes: Legal foundation to cancel agreements and recover damages when sellers or commercial partners deliberately hide major structural defects or financial liabilities.
17.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

23.official_section_title: What considerations and objects are lawful, and what not
23.official_text: The consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless— it is forbidden by law; or is of such a nature that, if permitted, it would defeat the provisions of any law; or is fraudulent; or involves or implies injury to the person or property of another; or the Court regards it as immoral, or opposed to public policy. In each of these cases, the consideration or object of an agreement is said to be unlawful. Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.
23.simplified_explanation: Declares that any agreement whose purpose or consideration violates statutory law, is fraudulent, causes injury, or opposes public policy is completely void from the beginning.
23.applicability_notes: Nullifies illegal contract clauses, predatory loan penalties, and unlawful employer bond agreements that contradict public statutes.
23.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
23.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

28.official_section_title: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void
28.official_text: Every agreement,— (a) by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time within which he may thus enforce his rights; or (b) which extinguishes the rights of any party thereto, or discharges any party thereto, from any liability, under or in respect of any contract on the expiry of a specified period so as to restrict any party from enforcing his rights, is void to that extent.
28.simplified_explanation: Declares completely void any contract clause that bars a party from approaching the courts or curtails the statutory limitation period.
28.applicability_notes: Protects contracting parties against unfair forfeiture clauses or clauses attempting to extinguish legal remedies earlier than the Limitation Act.
28.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
28.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

124.official_text: A contract by which one party promises to save the other from loss caused to him by the conduct of the promisor himself, or by the conduct of any other person, is called a 'contract of indemnity'.
124.simplified_explanation: Defines an indemnity contract where one party legally promises to protect and reimburse the other against losses caused by their own actions or third parties.
124.applicability_notes: Underpins commercial vendor agreements, service-level guarantees, and IP liability protection disputes between businesses and contractors.
124.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

25.official_section_title: Agreement without consideration, void, unless it is in writing and registered, or is a promise to compensate for something done, or is a promise to pay a debt barred by limitation law
25.official_text: An agreement made without consideration is void, unless— (1) it is expressed in writing and registered under the law for the time being in force for the registration of documents, and is made on account of natural love and affection between parties standing in a near relation to each other; or (2) it is a promise to compensate, wholly or in part, a person who has already voluntarily done something for the promisor; or (3) it is a promise, made in writing and signed by the person to be charged therewith, or by his agent generally or specially authorized in that behalf, to pay wholly or in part a debt of which the creditor might have enforced payment but for the law for the limitation of suits.
25.simplified_explanation: While agreements without consideration are generally void, a written and signed promise to pay a time-barred debt (under Section 25(3)) is fully valid and legally enforceable in a court of law.
25.applicability_notes: Invoked when a debtor provides a written undertaking or promissory note acknowledging and promising to repay an expired debt after the 3-year limitation period.
25.citation: Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Act No. 9 of 1872), s. 25
25.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

40.official_section_title: Person by whom promise is to be performed
40.official_text: If it appears from the nature of the case that it was the intention of the parties to any contract that any promise contained in it should be performed by the promisor himself, such promise must be performed by the promisor. In other cases, the promisor or his representatives may employ a competent person to perform it.
40.simplified_explanation: Specifies that where a contract involves personal skill, expertise, or trust, the obligation must be performed personally by the promisor and cannot be secretly subcontracted or delegated.
40.applicability_notes: Applies when professional service providers (architects, software developers, bespoke designers) secretly outsource contractual work to unqualified third parties without client consent.
40.citation: Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Act No. 9 of 1872), s. 40
40.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

55.official_section_title: Effect of failure to perform at fixed time, in contract in which time is essential
55.official_text: When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract.
55.simplified_explanation: Provides that when time is of the essence of an agreement, failure by a party to perform by the agreed deadline makes the contract voidable at the option of the other party, who can cancel and claim damages.
55.applicability_notes: Governs time-critical contracts such as exhibition stalls, wedding arrangements, seasonal event fabrications, and time-bound supply shipments.
55.citation: Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Act No. 9 of 1872), s. 55
55.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
55.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

151.official_section_title: Care to be taken by bailee
151.official_text: In all cases of bailment, the bailee is bound to take as much care of the goods bailed to him as a man of ordinary prudence would, under similar circumstances, take of his own goods of the same bulk, quantity and value as the goods bailed.
151.simplified_explanation: Establishes a mandatory duty of care for anyone entrusted with custody of goods (bailee) to treat the property with the same prudence as their own, regardless of unilateral disclaimer slips.
151.applicability_notes: Standard basis for liability in valet parking car crashes, dry-cleaner damage, cloakroom losses, and repair garage custody under Supreme Court of India jurisprudence.
151.citation: Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Act No. 9 of 1872), s. 151
151.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

10.official_text: All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void.
10.simplified_explanation: Establishes the fundamental requirements of an enforceable legal contract: mutual free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration, and a lawful objective.
10.applicability_notes: Foundational provision invoked to verify whether any commercial, rental, or freelance arrangement constitutes an enforceable legal contract.

11.official_text: Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject.
11.simplified_explanation: Specifies that only individuals of sound mind who have attained the age of majority (18 years) and are not disqualified by law can enter into legally binding contracts.
11.applicability_notes: Applies when challenging agreements signed by minors or persons lacking mental capacity.

62.official_section_title: Effect of novation, rescission, and alteration of contract
62.official_text: If the parties to a contract agree to substitute a new contract for it, or to rescind or alter it, the original contract need not be performed.
62.simplified_explanation: Provides that contracts can only be modified, rescinded, or novated by mutual agreement of all parties; unilateral alterations by one party are legally ineffective.
62.applicability_notes: Protects against unilateral changes in payment terms, timelines, or deliverables by one party without the other's consent.

64.official_section_title: Consequences of rescission of a voidable contract
64.official_text: When a person at whose option a contract is voidable rescinds it, the other party thereto need not perform any promise therein contained in which he is the promisor. The party rescinding a voidable contract shall, if he have received any benefit thereunder from another party to such contract, restore such benefit, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received.
64.simplified_explanation: Requires any party who rescinds a voidable contract (e.g., signed under coercion, fraud, or misrepresentation) to return and restore any advances, deposits, or benefits received.
64.applicability_notes: Governs restitution and refund of advances when a contract is rescinded due to misrepresentation, fraud, or coercion.

148.official_text: A 'bailment' is the delivery of goods by one person to another for some purpose, upon a contract that they shall, when the purpose is accomplished, be returned or otherwise disposed of according to the directions of the person delivering them. The person delivering the goods is called the 'bailor'. The person to whom they are delivered is called the 'bailee'.
148.simplified_explanation: Defines legal bailment when goods or vehicles are entrusted to another party (such as a valet service, garage, or warehouse) under an obligation to safely return them.
148.applicability_notes: Governs legal liability when entrusted goods, valet-parked cars, or repair items are damaged or lost.

152.official_section_title: Bailee when not liable for loss, etc., of thing bailed
152.official_text: The bailee, in the absence of any special contract, is not responsible for the loss, destruction or deterioration of the thing bailed, if he has taken the amount of care of it described in section 151.
152.simplified_explanation: Establishes that a custodian or bailee is strictly liable for loss or damage to bailed goods unless they prove they exercised standard prudent care.
152.applicability_notes: Used to invalidate unfair 'owner's risk' disclaimers when vehicles or goods in custodial care suffer damage.
152.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

170.official_text: Where the bailee has, in accordance with the purpose of the bailment, rendered any service involving the exercise of labour or skill in respect of the goods bailed, he has, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, a right to retain such goods until he receives due remuneration for the services he has rendered in respect of them.
170.simplified_explanation: Provides service providers, repair technicians, and artisans the right to retain possession of repaired goods until their legitimate service fee is paid.

126.official_text: A 'contract of guarantee' is a contract to perform the promise, or discharge the liability, of a third person in case of his default. The person who gives the guarantee is called the 'surety'; the person in respect of whose default the guarantee is given is called the 'principal debtor', and the person to whom the guarantee is given is called the 'creditor'.
126.simplified_explanation: Defines legal guarantee and surety obligations, confirming that a guarantor's liability only arises upon actual default by the principal debtor.
126.applicability_notes: Applies when loan apps, banks, or lenders harass third-party references or guarantors without establishing principal borrower default.

63.official_section_title: Promisee may dispense with or remit performance of promise
63.official_text: Every promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, the performance of the promise made to him, or may extend the time for such performance, or may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit.
63.simplified_explanation: Allows a party to whom performance is owed to waive or remit performance, extend time for delivery, or accept alternative satisfaction without requiring fresh consideration.
63.applicability_notes: Governs contractual milestone waivers, unconditional delivery date extensions, and negotiated settlements without new consideration.
63.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
