63.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

14.official_text: Consent is said to be free when it is not caused by— (1) coercion, as defined in section 15, or (2) undue influence, as defined in section 16, or (3) fraud, as defined in section 17, or (4) misrepresentation, as defined in section 18, or (5) mistake, subject to the provisions of sections 20, 21 and 22. Consent is said to be so caused when it would not have been given but for the existence of such coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation or mistake.
14.simplified_explanation: Establishes that a valid contract requires genuine free consent. If consent was obtained through coercion, pressure, fraud, false representations, or factual mistake, the contract is legally flawed and voidable.
legal_ingredients: Agreement entered into between parties
Absence of coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, or bilateral mistake of fact
14.punishment_or_remedy: Contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was vitiated under Section 19.
exceptions_and_limitations: If party had the means of discovering the truth with ordinary diligence in cases of misrepresentation.
14.applicability_notes: The foundation stone of Indian contract law; protects citizens coerced into signing one-sided indemnity bonds or unfair agreements.

20.official_section_title: Agreement void where both parties are under mistake as to matter of fact
20.official_text: Where both the parties to an agreement are under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement, the agreement is void. Explanation.—An erroneous opinion as to the value of the thing which forms the subject-matter of the agreement is not to be deemed a mistake as to a matter of fact.
20.simplified_explanation: Renders an agreement completely void from the beginning if both parties entered into it under a mutual mistake regarding a fundamental factual matter essential to the contract (e.g. goods already destroyed unknown to both).
legal_ingredients: Bilateral mistake common to both parties
Mistake relates to an essential matter of fact, not mere opinion of value
20.punishment_or_remedy: Agreement void ab initio; restoration of advantages or money under Section 65.
exceptions_and_limitations: A mistake as to market price or commercial profitability does not void the agreement.
20.applicability_notes: Enables citizens to escape accidental or impossible contracts and recover advance deposits.

21.official_section_title: Effect of mistakes as to law
21.official_text: A contract is not voidable because it was caused by a mistake as to any law in force in India; but a mistake as to a law not in force in India has the same effect as a mistake of fact.
21.simplified_explanation: Reaffirms the universal legal maxim that ignorance or mistake of Indian domestic law does not excuse non-performance or void a contract (ignorantia juris non excusat).
legal_ingredients: Mistake relating to a law in force in India
Contract remains fully valid and binding despite party's misconception of law
21.punishment_or_remedy: Contract remains enforceable; party cannot escape contractual performance on plea of ignorance of law.
exceptions_and_limitations: A mistake regarding foreign law is treated as a mistake of fact under the proviso.
21.applicability_notes: Parties cannot evade commercial contracts by claiming they were unaware of Indian statutory regulations.

32.official_section_title: Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event happening
32.official_text: Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event happens cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened. If the event becomes impossible, such contracts become void.
32.simplified_explanation: Governs contingent contracts: an agreement conditional on an uncertain future event (e.g. obtaining bank loan approval or municipal building sanction) cannot be legally enforced until that condition occurs, and becomes void if the condition becomes impossible.
legal_ingredients: Contract expressly dependent on collateral uncertain future event
Condition precedent must occur before performance can be demanded
Contract becomes void if the event becomes impossible
32.punishment_or_remedy: Contract becomes void upon impossibility; refund of advance deposits under Section 65.
exceptions_and_limitations: If the promisor himself wrongfully prevented the contingent event from happening, he cannot benefit from non-occurrence.
32.applicability_notes: Protects buyers who paid token advances subject to bank loan approval or legal clearance.

51.official_section_title: Promisor not bound to perform, unless reciprocal promisee ready and willing to perform
51.official_text: When a contract consists of reciprocal promises to be simultaneously performed, no promisor need perform his promise unless the promisee is ready and willing to perform his reciprocal promise.
51.simplified_explanation: Establishes the doctrine of concurrent conditions: in contracts with simultaneous promises (e.g. cash on delivery, or deed execution upon balance payment), neither party is bound to perform unless the other party is genuinely ready and willing to perform their part.
legal_ingredients: Reciprocal promises intended to be performed simultaneously
Promisor excused from performing if reciprocal promisee is unready or unwilling
51.punishment_or_remedy: Lawful withholding of performance; defense against breach of contract claim.
exceptions_and_limitations: Where contract expressly specifies an agreed order of performance.
51.applicability_notes: Allows software freelancers, suppliers, and service providers to withhold delivery if client refuses milestone payment.

67.official_section_title: Effect of neglect of promisee to afford promisor reasonable facilities for performance
67.official_text: If any promisee neglects or refuses to afford the promisor reasonable facilities for the performance of his promise, the promisor is excused by such neglect or refusal as to any non-performance caused thereby.
67.simplified_explanation: Excuses a contractor, vendor, or freelancer from liability for delay or non-performance if the client failed to provide necessary approvals, server access, raw materials, or site clearance needed to do the job.
legal_ingredients: Contract requires cooperation or facility from promisee (access, designs, inputs)
Promisee neglects or refuses to provide reasonable facilities
Promisor excused from non-performance or delay caused by promisee default
67.punishment_or_remedy: Promisor excused from contractual breach; right to claim compensation for expenses incurred.
exceptions_and_limitations: Promisor must prove that written requests for facilities or access were made and ignored.
67.applicability_notes: Protects IT agencies and independent contractors from liquidated damages when client ghosted or delayed approvals.

172.official_text: The bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise is called "pledge". The bailor is in this case called the "pawnor". The bailee is called the "pawnee".
172.simplified_explanation: Defines a pledge: the bailment of gold, physical goods, or securities to a lender as collateral security for a loan or debt. The borrower is the pawnor, and the lender/bank is the pawnee.
legal_ingredients: Bailment and transfer of possession of movable goods
Goods transferred as security for payment of debt or performance of promise
172.punishment_or_remedy: Governs statutory rights and obligations between gold loan borrowers and NBFCs/pawnbrokers.
exceptions_and_limitations: Pledge requires actual or constructive delivery of possession of goods to pawnee.
172.applicability_notes: Applies to gold loans, share pledges, vehicle pawn loans, and banking collateral disputes.

176.official_section_title: Pawnee's right where pawnor makes default
176.official_text: If the pawnor makes default in payment of the debt, or performance, at the stipulated time or the promise, in respect of which the goods were pledged, the pawnee may bring a suit against the pawnor upon the debt or promise, and retain the goods pledged as a collateral security; or he may sell the thing pledged, on giving the pawnor reasonable notice of the sale. If the proceeds of such sale are less than the amount due in respect of the debt or promise, the pawnor is still liable to pay the balance. If the proceeds of the sale are greater than the amount so due, the pawnee shall pay over the surplus to the pawnor.
176.simplified_explanation: Mandates that if a borrower defaults on a gold loan or pledged collateral, the lender CANNOT secretly sell the pledged goods. The lender MUST give reasonable written notice of auction to the borrower and must immediately refund any surplus proceeds.
legal_ingredients: Borrower default in repayment of pledged debt
Mandatory statutory requirement: pawnee MUST give reasonable written notice of sale to pawnor
Obligation to return surplus sale proceeds to borrower
176.punishment_or_remedy: Sale conducted without reasonable notice is illegal conversion; borrower entitled to return of gold or damages.
exceptions_and_limitations: Notice of sale cannot be waived even by express contractual clause (Apex Court in PTC India Financial Services v. Venkateswarlu).
176.amendment_status: In force; non-waivability of notice affirmed by Supreme Court.
176.applicability_notes: Vital protection against aggressive NBFCs and gold loan companies secretly auctioning family gold without statutory notice.

4.official_text: (1) Gratuity shall be payable to an employee on the termination of his employment after he has rendered continuous service for not less than five years, — (a) on his superannuation, or (b) on his retirement or resignation, or (c) on his death or disablement due to accident or disease: Provided that the completion of continuous service of five years shall not be necessary where the termination of the employment of any employee is due to death or disablement... (2) For every completed year of service or part thereof in excess of six months, the employer shall pay gratuity to an employee at the rate of fifteen days' wages based on the rate of wages last drawn by the employee concerned.
4.simplified_explanation: Mandates that any employee who has completed five years of continuous service is legally entitled to gratuity upon resignation, retirement, or termination, calculated at fifteen days' wages for every completed year of service.
4.applicability_notes: Applies when an employer refuses or fails to pay statutory gratuity after an employee resigns or is terminated after five or more years of service.
4.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
4.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

7.official_section_title: Determination of the amount of gratuity
7.official_text: (1) A person who is eligible for payment of gratuity under this Act or any person authorised, in writing, to act on his behalf shall send a written application to the employer... (2) As soon as gratuity becomes payable, the employer shall, whether an application referred to in sub-section (1) has been made or not, determine the amount of gratuity and give notice in writing to the person to whom the gratuity is payable and also to the controlling authority specifying the amount of gratuity so determined. (3) The employer shall arrange to pay the amount of gratuity within thirty days from the date it becomes payable to the person to whom the gratuity is payable. (3A) If the amount of gratuity payable under sub-section (3) is not paid by the employer within the period specified in sub-section (3), the employer shall pay, from the date on which the gratuity becomes payable to the date on which it is paid, simple interest at such rate, not exceeding the rate notified by the Central Government.
7.simplified_explanation: Requires the employer to determine and disburse the gratuity amount within thirty days of it becoming payable, and mandates payment of simple interest (currently 10% per annum) for any delay in disbursement.
7.applicability_notes: Applies when an employer delays gratuity disbursement beyond 30 days without lawful justification.
7.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
7.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

8.official_text: If the amount of gratuity payable under this Act is not paid by the employer, within the prescribed time, to the person entitled thereto, the controlling authority shall, on an application made to it in this behalf by the aggrieved person, issue a certificate for that amount to the Collector, who shall recover the same, together with compound interest thereon as arrears of land revenue and pay the same to the person entitled thereto.
8.simplified_explanation: Empowers the Controlling Authority to issue a recovery certificate to the District Collector to recover unpaid gratuity from the employer as arrears of land revenue with compound interest.
8.applicability_notes: Used to legally enforce recovery of unpaid gratuity through revenue authorities against defaulting employers.
8.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
8.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

14.official_text: The provisions of this Act or any rule made thereunder shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any enactment other than this Act or in any instrument or contract having effect by virtue of any enactment other than this Act.
14.simplified_explanation: Provides that statutory gratuity rights override any inconsistent employment agreement, company policy, or internal waiver signed by the employee.
14.applicability_notes: Prevents employers from relying on employment contract clauses or bond waivers to deny statutory gratuity.
14.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
14.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

5.official_section_title: Right to payment of maternity benefit
5.official_text: (1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, every woman shall be entitled to, and her employer shall be liable for, the payment of maternity benefit at the rate of the average daily wage for the period of her actual absence... (2) No woman shall be entitled to maternity benefit unless she has actually worked in an establishment of the employer from whom she claims maternity benefit, for a period of not less than eighty days in the twelve months immediately preceding the date of her expected delivery... (3) The maximum period for which any woman shall be entitled to maternity benefit shall be twenty-six weeks of which not more than eight weeks shall precede the date of her expected delivery.
5.simplified_explanation: Grants female employees who have worked at least 80 days the statutory right to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave at the rate of full average daily wages.
5.applicability_notes: Primary section when an employer refuses paid maternity leave or withholds salary during statutory maternity leave.
5.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
5.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

12.official_section_title: Dismissal during absence of pregnancy to be void
12.official_text: (1) When a woman absents herself from work in accordance with the provisions of this Act, it shall be unlawful for her employer to discharge or dismiss her during or on account of such absence, or to give notice of discharge or dismissal on such a day that the notice will expire during such absence, or to vary to her disadvantage any of the conditions of her service.
12.simplified_explanation: Explicitly declares any discharge, dismissal, termination, or disadvantageous variation of service conditions of a female employee during pregnancy or maternity leave to be completely unlawful and void.
12.applicability_notes: Applies when an employer terminates or threatens an employee due to pregnancy or during her maternity absence.
12.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
12.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

epf_act_1952.official_act_name: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

6.official_section_title: Contributions and matters which may be provided for in Schemes
6.official_text: The contribution which shall be paid by the employer to the Fund shall be ten per cent. (or twelve per cent. where applicable) of the basic wages, dearness allowance and retaining allowance for the time being payable to each of the employees, and the employee's contribution shall be equal to the contribution payable by the employer in respect of him.
6.simplified_explanation: Mandates the statutory deduction of Provident Fund contributions (typically 12%) from employee wages and requires an equal matching contribution from the employer.
6.applicability_notes: Governs mandatory employer and employee PF contributions and prohibits evasion of statutory provident fund obligations.
6.citation: Section 6, Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
6.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
6.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

7A.official_section_title: Determination of moneys due from employers
7A.official_text: (1) The Central Provident Fund Commissioner, any Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner, any Deputy Provident Fund Commissioner, any Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, or any Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner may, by order, — (a) in a case where a dispute arises regarding the applicability of this Act to an establishment, decide such dispute; and (b) determine the amount due from any employer under any provision of this Act... and for this purpose may conduct such inquiry as he may deem necessary.
7A.simplified_explanation: Empowers Regional Provident Fund Commissioners to conduct formal inquiries, summon employer records, determine unpaid PF dues, and order statutory recovery against defaulting employers.
7A.applicability_notes: Primary mechanism for employees to report defaulting employers to EPFO for assessment and coercive recovery.
7A.citation: Section 7A, Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
7A.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

14.official_text: (1) Whoever, for the purpose of avoiding any payment to be made by himself under this Act, the Scheme, the Pension Scheme or the Insurance Scheme... makes or causes to be made any false statement or false representation shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine... (1A) An employer who contravenes, or makes default in complying with, the provisions of section 6 or clause (a) of sub-section (3) of section 17... shall be punishable with imprisonment.
14.simplified_explanation: Prescribes criminal penalties and imprisonment for employers who deduct PF from employees' pay and fail to remit it to EPFO or make false declarations.
14.applicability_notes: Establishes criminal liability for non-remittance of deducted employee provident fund money.
14.citation: Section 14, Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
14.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
14.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

14B.official_text: Where an employer makes default in the payment of any contribution to the Fund, the Pension Fund or the Insurance Fund or in the transfer of accumulations required to be transferred by him... the Central Provident Fund Commissioner or such other officer as may be authorised... may recover from the employer by way of penalty such damages, not exceeding the amount of arrears, as may be specified in the Scheme...
14B.simplified_explanation: Empowers EPFO recovery officers to impose penal damages and recover unpaid provident fund arrears directly from defaulting employers.
14B.applicability_notes: Statutory weapon deployed against employers who deduct employee PF share but fail to deposit accumulations with EPFO.
14B.citation: Section 14B, Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
14B.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

10.official_section_title: Specific performance in respect of contracts
10.official_text: The specific performance of a contract shall be enforced by the court subject to the provisions contained in sub-section (2) of section 11, section 14 and section 16.
10.simplified_explanation: Mandates that courts shall order specific performance of a contract, directing the defaulting party to fulfill their exact agreed contractual obligations rather than merely awarding damages, especially in property or unique commercial transactions.
10.applicability_notes: Applies when a party seeks actual fulfillment of agreed promises such as property sale, lease handover, or unique deliverable execution.
10.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
10.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

20.official_text: (1) Where the contract is broken due to the non-performance of promise by any party, the party who suffers by such breach shall have the option of substituted performance through a third party or by his own agency, and, recover the expenses and other costs actually incurred, spent or suffered by him, from the party committing such breach. (2) No substituted performance shall be undertaken unless the party who suffers such breach has given a notice in writing of not less than thirty days to the party in breach.
20.simplified_explanation: Allows an aggrieved party, after giving 30 days written notice to the breaching contractor, to get the unfinished or defective work completed through a third party and recover all incurred costs and expenses from the defaulting contractor.
20.applicability_notes: Critical remedy for abandoned renovation work, unfinished construction, and vendor service defaults.
20.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
20.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

38.official_text: (1) Subject to the other provisions contained in or referred to by this Chapter, a perpetual injunction may be granted to the plaintiff to prevent the breach of an obligation existing in his favour, whether expressly or by implication. (2) When any such obligation arises from contract, the court shall be guided by the rules and provisions contained in Chapter II.
38.simplified_explanation: Empowers courts to grant permanent injunctions restraining a contracting party from committing a breach of contract or continuing an unlawful act.
38.applicability_notes: Used to restrain contract violations, unauthorized sub-leasing, misuse of confidential assets, or ongoing breach of agreements.
38.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
38.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

14.official_text: The following contracts cannot be specifically enforced, namely:— (a) where a party to the contract has obtained substituted performance of contract in accordance with the provisions of section 20; (b) a contract, the performance of which involves the performance of a continuous duty which the court cannot supervise; (c) a contract which is so dependent on the personal qualifications of the parties that the court cannot enforce specific performance of its material terms; and (d) a contract which is in its nature determinable.
14.simplified_explanation: Specifies contracts that courts cannot order specific performance for: contracts where substituted performance was taken, personal service/employment contracts, contracts requiring continuous court supervision, and contracts that can be terminated by either party (determinable).
legal_ingredients: Contract falls into statutory exclusion categories
Remedy restricted to monetary compensation/damages rather than specific performance
14.punishment_or_remedy: Dismissal of specific performance suit; court awards monetary damages under Section 73 Contract Act.
exceptions_and_limitations: Contracts for transfer of immovable property are generally enforceable under Section 10.
14.amendment_status: In force; substituted by Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2018.
14.applicability_notes: Employers cannot force employees to work, nor can agency partners force personal services under this section.

16.official_text: Specific performance of a contract cannot be enforced in favour of a person— (a) who has obtained substituted performance of contract under section 20; or (b) who has become incapable of performing, or violates any essential term of, the contract... or acts in fraud of the contract... or (c) who fails to prove that he has performed or has always been ready and willing to perform the essential terms of the contract which are to be performed by him.
16.simplified_explanation: Mandates that a buyer seeking specific performance of a property sale agreement MUST prove continuous 'readiness and willingness' (financial capacity and intent to pay) from the date of the agreement until the trial.
legal_ingredients: Plaintiff in specific performance suit
Mandatory statutory requirement: proof of continuous readiness (financial capacity) and willingness (mental intent) to perform essential terms
Failure to prove continuous readiness is an absolute statutory bar
16.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory dismissal of specific performance suit if readiness and willingness is not proved.
exceptions_and_limitations: Readiness does not require carrying physical cash at all times; proving genuine financial capability (bank funds, sanctioned loan) is sufficient.
16.amendment_status: In force; 2018 amendment retained Section 16(c) readiness and willingness bar.
16.applicability_notes: Central battleground in all real estate and property sale agreement litigation in India.

41.official_text: An injunction cannot be granted— (e) to prevent the breach of a contract the performance of which would not be specifically enforced; (h) when equally efficacious relief can certainly be obtained by any other usual mode of proceeding except in case of breach of trust; (i) when the conduct of the plaintiff or his agents has been such as to disentitle him to the assistance of the court; (j) when the plaintiff has no personal interest in the matter.
41.simplified_explanation: Sets out statutory bars where civil courts cannot grant injunctions: when money damages would be equally efficacious, when the contract itself is not specifically enforceable, or when the plaintiff has unclean hands.
legal_ingredients: Suit for permanent or temporary injunction
Equally efficacious alternative relief (e.g. monetary damages) available
Or plaintiff's own inequitable conduct disentitles relief
41.punishment_or_remedy: Refusal and dismissal of injunction application.
exceptions_and_limitations: Does not apply to clear breaches of trust.
41.applicability_notes: Prevents parties from obtaining frivolous stay orders when their losses can easily be compensated in money.

18.official_text: (1) No person shall manufacture, pack, sell, import, distribute, deliver, offer, expose or possess for sale any pre-packaged commodity, unless such package is in such standard quantities or number and bears thereon such declarations and particulars in such manner as may be prescribed.
18.simplified_explanation: Mandates that every pre-packaged product sold in India or online must clearly display the Maximum Retail Price (MRP), net quantity, manufacturing date, expiry date, and manufacturer/importer contact details.
18.applicability_notes: Primary statutory provision violated when sellers conceal MRP, tamper with package labels, or fail to declare net quantity on packaged goods.
18.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
18.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

36.official_section_title: Penalty for selling, etc., of non-standard packages
36.official_text: (1) Whoever manufactures, packs, imports, sells, distributes, delivers or offers for sale any pre-packaged commodity which does not conform to the declarations on the package as provided in this Act shall be punished with fine which may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees, for the second offence, with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees and for the subsequent offence, with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to one lakh rupees or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with both.
36.simplified_explanation: Imposes strict financial penalties up to one lakh rupees and imprisonment for selling goods above MRP, tampering with price tags, or selling non-standard packages.
36.applicability_notes: Applies to retail stores, cinema halls, airports, and restaurants charging prices above the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) printed on packaged beverages and goods.
36.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

26.official_section_title: Responsibilities of the food business operator
26.official_text: (1) Every food business operator shall ensure that the articles of food satisfy the requirements of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder at all stages of production, processing, import, distribution and sale within the businesses under his control.
26.simplified_explanation: Places strict legal responsibility on restaurants, cloud kitchens, and food delivery platforms to ensure that food items are safe, hygienic, and free from contaminants at all stages.
26.applicability_notes: Directly applies to food quality failures, spoiled food deliveries, and unhygienic restaurant kitchens.
26.citation: Section 26, Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
26.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
26.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

50.official_section_title: Penalty for selling food not of the nature or substance or quality demanded
50.official_text: Any person who sells to the purchaser's prejudice any food which is not in compliance with the provisions of this Act or the regulations made thereunder, or of the nature or substance or quality demanded by the purchaser, shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees.
50.simplified_explanation: Imposes a fine of up to five lakh rupees on food operators who sell food that does not match the promised quality, nature, or dietary specifications.
50.applicability_notes: Applies when food ordered is stale, substituted with substandard ingredients, or fails nutritional claims.
50.citation: Section 50, Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
50.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
50.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.

59.official_text: Any person who, whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf, manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption which is unsafe, shall be punishable, — (i) where such failure or contravention does not result in injury, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and also with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees; (ii) where such failure results in a non-grievous injury, with imprisonment up to one year and fine up to three lakh rupees; (iii) where causing grievous injury, with imprisonment up to six years; (iv) where causing death, with imprisonment for life.
59.simplified_explanation: Prescribes severe criminal penalties and imprisonment up to life for selling unsafe or contaminated food that endangers health or causes injury.
59.applicability_notes: Applies to food poisoning incidents, foreign objects (insects, glass, nails) in restaurant food, and hazardous chemical contamination.
59.citation: Section 59, Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
59.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
59.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

65.official_section_title: Compensation in case of injury or death of consumer
65.official_text: (1) Without prejudice to the other provisions of this Chapter, if any person whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf, manufactures or distributes or sells or imports any article of food which causes injury to the consumer or his death, it shall be lawful for the Adjudicating Officer or as the case may be, the Court, to direct him to pay compensation to the victim or the legal representative of the victims, a sum — (a) not less than five lakh rupees in case of death; (b) not exceeding three lakh rupees in case of grievous injury; and (c) not exceeding one lakh rupees in all other cases of injury.
65.simplified_explanation: Mandates payment of direct statutory compensation up to five lakh rupees to consumers or their families who suffer bodily injury or food poisoning from contaminated food.
65.applicability_notes: Provides a direct statutory compensation remedy for medical bills, hospitalization, and harm resulting from contaminated meals.
65.citation: Section 65, Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
65.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
65.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

51.official_text: Any person who whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption which is sub-standard, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to five lakh rupees.
51.simplified_explanation: Imposes a heavy statutory financial penalty of up to Rs 5 Lakh on food manufacturers, cloud kitchens, and restaurants that sell or deliver substandard food that fails statutory nutritional and purity standards.
legal_ingredients: Article of food intended for human consumption
Failure to meet prescribed quality standards or specifications
Penalty up to Rs 5,00,000 imposed by Adjudicating Officer
51.punishment_or_remedy: Penalty up to five lakh rupees.
exceptions_and_limitations: Penalty adjudicated by District Additional District Magistrate (ADM/Adjudicating Officer).
51.applicability_notes: Directly targets substandard commercial food, cloud kitchen meals, and adulterated food items.
51.citation: Section 51, Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006

52.official_text: (1) Any person who whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption which is misbranded, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to three lakh rupees... (2) The Adjudicating Officer may issue a direction to the person found guilty of an offence under this section, for taking corrective action.
52.simplified_explanation: Imposes a fine of up to Rs 3 Lakh on companies selling misbranded food items that carry misleading labels, false nutritional claims, or conceal artificial additives and preservatives.
legal_ingredients: Misbranded food with deceptive labels or false claims
Failure to disclose ingredients, allergens, or genuine nutritional values
Penalty up to Rs 3,00,000
52.punishment_or_remedy: Penalty up to three lakh rupees, plus recall of misbranded batches.
exceptions_and_limitations: Excludes minor typographical errors that do not mislead the consumer as to nature or quality.
52.applicability_notes: Protects consumers against 'health washing', fake organic claims, and hidden chemicals in packaged foods.
52.citation: Section 52, Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006

54.official_section_title: Penalty for food containing extraneous matter
54.official_text: Any person whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption containing extraneous matter, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to one lakh rupees.
54.simplified_explanation: Imposes a penalty of up to Rs 1 Lakh on any restaurant, cloud kitchen, or packaged food brand for serving or selling food containing foreign objects, insects, glass, plastic, or dead matter.
legal_ingredients: Presence of extraneous foreign matter (insects, glass, plastic, hair, stones) in food
Food intended for human consumption
Penalty up to Rs 1,00,000
54.punishment_or_remedy: Penalty up to one lakh rupees, food safety inspection, and consumer damages.
exceptions_and_limitations: Extraneous matter must not be inherent to the natural raw product (e.g., fruit seed).
54.applicability_notes: Frequently invoked when delivery meals or restaurant food contains insects, dead pests, or sharp objects.
54.citation: Section 54, Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006

13.official_section_title: No deposit or advance to be taken by promoter without first entering into agreement for sale
13.official_text: (1) A promoter shall not accept a sum more than ten per cent. of the cost of the apartment, plot, or building as the case may be, as an advance payment or an application fee, from a person without first entering into a written agreement for sale with such person and register the said agreement for sale.
13.simplified_explanation: Strictly prohibits real estate builders and developers from taking more than 10% of property cost as advance payment without executing a registered agreement for sale.
13.applicability_notes: Protects homebuyers from builders demanding huge cash advances or forfeiting token money without a registered contract.
13.citation: Section 13, Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016
13.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
13.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

14.official_section_title: Adherence to sanctioned plans and project specifications by the promoter
14.official_text: (1) The proposed project shall be developed and completed by the promoter in accordance with the sanctioned plans, layout plans and specifications as approved by the competent authorities. (3) In case any structural defect or any other defect in workmanship, quality or provision of services... is brought to the notice of the promoter within a period of five years by the allottee from the date of handing over possession, it shall be the duty of the promoter to rectify such defects without further charge, within thirty days.
14.simplified_explanation: Mandates that builders must adhere strictly to approved layouts and holds the developer liable for structural defects and poor workmanship for a period of five years after handing over possession.
14.applicability_notes: Applies to construction quality defects, ceiling leaks, wall cracks, and unauthorized alterations made by builders without homebuyer consent.
14.citation: Section 14, Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016
14.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
14.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

18.official_text: (1) If the promoter fails to complete or is unable to give possession of an apartment, plot or building, — (a) in accordance with the terms of the agreement for sale or, as the case may be, duly completed by the date specified therein... he shall be liable on demand to the allottees, in case the allottee wishes to withdraw from the project, without prejudice to any other remedy available, to return the amount received by him in respect of that apartment, plot, building, as the case may be, with interest at such rate as may be prescribed in this behalf including compensation.
18.simplified_explanation: Empowers homebuyers to demand a full refund of all amounts paid along with statutory interest (State SBI MCLR + 2%) and compensation if the builder delays possession beyond the agreed completion date.
18.applicability_notes: Foundational section invoked in real estate possession delay cases, builder project halts, and refund claims.
18.citation: Section 18, Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016
18.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
18.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

31.official_section_title: Filing of complaints with the Authority or the adjudicating officer
31.official_text: (1) Any aggrieved person may file a complaint with the Authority or the adjudicating officer, as the case may be, for any violation or contravention of the provisions of this Act or the rules and regulations made thereunder against any promoter allottee or real estate agent, as the case may be.
31.simplified_explanation: Establishes the statutory right of any aggrieved homebuyer to file an online complaint before the State RERA Authority or Adjudicating Officer for fast-track dispute resolution.
31.applicability_notes: Governs the statutory forum for filing complaints against fraudulent real estate developers, illegal advance forfeitures, and delayed handovers.
31.citation: Section 31, Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016
31.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
31.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

11.official_text: (1) The promoter shall, upon receiving his Login Id and password... create his web page on the website of the Authority and enter all details of the proposed project... (3) The promoter at the time of the booking and issue of allotment letter shall be responsible to make available to the allottee... sanctioned plans, layout plans... (4) The promoter shall— (a) be responsible for all obligations, responsibilities and functions under the provisions of this Act... till the conveyance of all the apartments, plots or buildings... (b) be responsible to obtain the completion certificate or the occupancy certificate, or both.
11.simplified_explanation: Mandates that real estate builders and promoters must disclose all project sanctions on the RERA website, provide sanctioned layouts at booking, and obtain official completion/occupancy certificates before handover.
legal_ingredients: Promoter developing real estate project exceeding 500 sq meters or 8 apartments
Statutory duty to upload quarterly project progress
Obligation to secure Occupancy Certificate (OC) prior to physical possession
11.punishment_or_remedy: RERA Authority directions, penalty up to 5% of estimated project cost under Section 61.
exceptions_and_limitations: Applies strictly to projects registered or registrable under RERA.
11.applicability_notes: Builders cannot offer possession on mere 'fit-out' basis without obtaining official completion/occupancy certificate.
11.citation: Section 11, Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016

12.official_section_title: Obligations of promoter regarding veracity of advertisement or prospectus
12.official_text: Where any person makes an advance or a deposit on the basis of the information contained in the notice, advertisement or prospectus, or on the basis of any model apartment, plot or building... and sustains any loss or damage by reason of any incorrect, false statement included therein, he shall be compensated by the promoter in the manner as provided under this Act: Provided that if the person affected by such incorrect, false statement contained in the notice, advertisement or prospectus, or the model apartment, plot or building, as the case may be, intends to withdraw from the proposed project, he shall be returned his entire investment along with interest at such rate as may be prescribed and the compensation in the manner provided under this Act.
12.simplified_explanation: Grants home buyers the statutory right to withdraw from a project and demand a 100% refund of their entire investment with interest and compensation if the builder lured them with false advertisements, fake amenities, or deceptive model apartments.
legal_ingredients: Deposit or advance made relying on builder's brochure, advertisement, or model flat
False, misleading, or incorrect statement in marketing materials
Allottee intention to withdraw from project or claim damages
12.punishment_or_remedy: Immediate full refund of all amounts paid plus statutory interest (MCLR + 2%) and compensation from promoter.
exceptions_and_limitations: Allottee must produce copy of advertisement, brochure, or email representations relied upon.
12.applicability_notes: Potent statutory protection against real estate 'flyer deception', phantom amenities, and bait-and-switch layout changes.
12.citation: Section 12, Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016

19.official_text: (1) The allottee shall be entitled to obtain the information relating to sanctioned plans, layout plans... (3) The allottee shall be entitled to claim the possession of apartment, plot or building... (4) The allottee shall be entitled to claim the refund of amount paid along with interest at such rate as may be prescribed and compensation in the manner as provided under this Act, from the promoter, if the promoter fails to comply or is unable to give possession of the apartment, plot or building in accordance with the terms of agreement for sale... (6) Every allottee, who has entered into an agreement for sale... shall be responsible to make necessary payments in the manner and within the time as specified in the said agreement for sale.
19.simplified_explanation: Defines mutual rights and duties: home buyers have the statutory right to timely possession, project information, and full refund with interest if possession is delayed, while having a duty to pay construction-linked installments on time.
legal_ingredients: Allottee under registered agreement for sale
Right to timely possession as per agreed date
Promoter default triggers statutory right to refund with interest or monthly delay interest
19.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory refund or monthly interest until actual delivery of physical possession.
exceptions_and_limitations: Allottee who defaults in timely milestone payments may be liable to pay delay interest to the promoter.
19.applicability_notes: Statutory benchmark balancing buyer rights with installment payment obligations.
19.citation: Section 19, Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016

43.official_section_title: Establishment of Real Estate Appellate Tribunal
43.official_text: (1) The appropriate Government shall, by notification, establish an Appellate Tribunal to be known as the — (name of the State/Union territory) Real Estate Appellate Tribunal... (5) Any person aggrieved by any direction or decision or order made by the Authority or by an adjudicating officer under this Act may prefer an appeal before the Appellate Tribunal having jurisdiction... Provided that where a promoter files an appeal with the Appellate Tribunal, it shall not be entertained, without the promoter first having deposited with the Appellate Tribunal at least thirty per cent. of the penalty, or such higher percentage as may be determined... or the total amount to be paid to the allottee including interest and compensation.
43.simplified_explanation: Establishes the Real Estate Appellate Tribunal (REAT) to hear appeals within 60 days. Builders appealing a refund order must pre-deposit 100% of the amount awarded to the allottee (or 30% of penalty), preventing delay tactics.
legal_ingredients: Appeal preferred within 60 days of RERA Authority order
Promoter appellant must pre-deposit 100% of awarded allottee refund/compensation (Newtech Promoters v. State of UP)
43.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory appeal; mandatory 100% pre-deposit locks builder money for consumer benefit.
exceptions_and_limitations: Delay beyond 60 days can be condoned only on proving sufficient cause.
43.amendment_status: In force; 100% pre-deposit upheld by Supreme Court in Newtech Promoters (2021).
43.applicability_notes: High Court level appellate oversight; strict pre-deposit requirement protects home buyers from endless builder litigation.
43.citation: Section 43, Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016

16.official_section_title: Implied conditions as to quality or fitness
16.official_text: Subject to the provisions of this Act and of any other law for the time being in force, there is no implied warranty or condition as to the quality or fitness for any particular purpose of goods supplied under a contract of sale, except as follows: — (1) Where the buyer, expressly or by implication, makes known to the seller the particular purpose for which the goods are required, so as to show that the buyer relies on the seller's skill or judgment... there is an implied condition that the goods shall be reasonably fit for such purpose.
16.simplified_explanation: Establishes the fundamental legal condition that goods supplied must be reasonably fit for their intended purpose and of merchantable quality when bought from a dealer.
16.applicability_notes: Governs commercial supply contracts and B2B goods purchases where delivered machinery, parts, or materials fail operational specifications.
16.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
16.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

31.official_text: It is the duty of the seller to deliver the goods and of the buyer to accept and pay for them, in accordance with the terms of the contract of sale.
31.simplified_explanation: Defines the concurrent legal duties of the seller to deliver the agreed goods and of the buyer to make payment under the contract.
31.applicability_notes: Applies to disputes over non-delivery of purchased goods, refusal to accept delivery, or payment default.
31.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
31.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

57.official_text: Where the seller wrongfully neglects or refuses to deliver the goods to the buyer, the buyer may sue the seller for damages for non-delivery.
57.simplified_explanation: Gives commercial buyers the right to sue the seller for damages and market price differential when the supplier fails or refuses to deliver contracted goods.
57.applicability_notes: Directly applied when vendors fail to ship raw materials or supplies after accepting orders, forcing buyers to purchase from the open market at higher cost.
57.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
57.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

59.official_text: (1) Where there is a breach of warranty by the seller, or where the buyer elects or is compelled to treat any breach of a condition on the part of the seller as a breach of warranty, the buyer is not by reason only of such breach of warranty entitled to reject the goods; but he may— (a) set up against the seller the breach of warranty in diminution or extinction of the price; or (b) sue the seller for damages for breach of warranty.
59.simplified_explanation: Gives the buyer the legal right to reduce or extinguish the purchase price or sue the seller for damages when supplied commercial goods fail warranty standards.
59.applicability_notes: Statutory remedy for defective industrial fasteners, broken machine components, and non-conforming commercial supplies.
59.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
59.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

12.official_text: (1) A stipulation in a contract of sale with reference to goods which are the subject thereof may be a condition or a warranty. (2) A condition is a stipulation essential to the main purpose of the contract, the breach of which gives rise to a right to treat the contract as repudiated. (3) A warranty is a stipulation collateral to the main purpose of the contract, the breach of which gives rise to a claim for damages but not to a right to reject the goods and treat the contract as repudiated. (4) Whether a stipulation in a contract of sale is a condition or a warranty depends in each case on the construction of the contract.
12.simplified_explanation: Distinguishes between a core Condition and a collateral Warranty: breach of a vital condition entitles the buyer to cancel the contract, reject the goods, and demand a full refund; breach of a warranty only entitles the buyer to claim financial damages.
legal_ingredients: Contract of sale of goods
Breach of condition: vital stipulation going to root of contract -> right to repudiate contract and reject goods
Breach of warranty: collateral term -> right to monetary damages only
12.punishment_or_remedy: Repudiation of contract and full refund for condition breach; compensation for warranty breach.
exceptions_and_limitations: Parties' use of the word 'condition' or 'warranty' in text is not conclusive; courts look at the substance of the agreement.
12.applicability_notes: Essential distinction in all commercial procurement, machinery supply, and commodity trading disputes.

13.official_section_title: When condition to be treated as warranty
13.official_text: (1) Where a contract of sale is subject to any condition to be fulfilled by the seller, the buyer may waive the condition or elect to treat the breach of the condition as a breach of warranty and not as a ground for treating the contract as repudiated. (2) Where a contract of sale is not severable and the buyer has accepted the goods or part thereof, the breach of any condition... can only be treated as a breach of warranty... unless there is a term of the contract, express or implied, to that effect.
13.simplified_explanation: Clarifies that if a buyer accepts goods or continues using them after discovering a defect, the law treats the breach of condition as a breach of warranty, restricting the buyer to claiming damages rather than rejecting the goods.
legal_ingredients: Buyer accepted goods or part thereof in non-severable contract
Buyer waiver of condition
Remedy converted from rejection of goods to action for damages
13.punishment_or_remedy: Damages in diminution of price under Section 59.
exceptions_and_limitations: Acceptance does not occur if buyer was not given a reasonable opportunity to examine goods under Section 41.
13.applicability_notes: Warns commercial buyers that using defective goods for months prevents them from demanding a total return.

14.official_section_title: Implied undertaking as to title, etc.
14.official_text: In a contract of sale, unless the circumstances of the contract are such as to show a different intention, there is— (a) an implied condition on the part of the seller that, in the case of a sale, he has a right to sell the goods... and (b) an implied warranty that the buyer shall have and enjoy quiet possession of the goods; (c) an implied warranty that the goods shall be free from any charge or encumbrance in favour of any third party not declared or known to the buyer.
14.simplified_explanation: Guarantees an automatic implied condition that the seller is the legal owner with the right to sell, and an implied warranty that the goods are free from undisclosed third-party loans, hypothecation, or legal claims.
legal_ingredients: Contract of sale of goods
Statutory implied condition that seller has lawful title to sell
Implied warranty of quiet possession and freedom from third-party charges
14.punishment_or_remedy: Repudiation of sale and full refund if seller had no title (Rowland v. Divall); damages for third party encumbrance.
exceptions_and_limitations: Excludes sales where seller purports to sell only such title as he or a third person may have.
14.applicability_notes: Protects buyers who unwittingly buy stolen goods, hypothecated vehicles, or goods with bank liens.

15.official_text: Where there is a contract for the sale of goods by description, there is an implied condition that the goods shall correspond with the description; and, if the sale is by sample as well as by description, it is not sufficient that the bulk of the goods corresponds with the sample if the goods do not also correspond with the description.
15.simplified_explanation: Mandates that when goods are sold by description (e.g. online catalog, technical specification, grade of steel/fabric), the delivered goods MUST correspond strictly with that description. If they differ, the buyer has the legal right to reject them.
legal_ingredients: Sale of goods by description or specification
Delivered goods fail to correspond with the agreed description
Breach of statutory implied condition
15.punishment_or_remedy: Right to reject delivered goods and claim complete refund of purchase price plus damages.
exceptions_and_limitations: De minimis non curat lex: microscopic deviations that do not affect utility or commercial description are disregarded.
15.applicability_notes: Foundation of commercial quality enforcement; seller cannot deliver a different brand, model, or grade than specified.

17.official_text: (1) A contract of sale is a contract for sale by sample where there is a term in the contract, express or implied, to that effect. (2) In the case of a contract for sale by sample there is an implied condition— (a) that the bulk shall correspond with the sample in quality; (b) that the buyer shall have a reasonable opportunity of comparing the bulk with the sample; (c) that the goods shall be free from any defect, rendering them unmerchantable, which would not be apparent on reasonable examination of the sample.
17.simplified_explanation: Requires that when goods are ordered based on a sample, the bulk shipment must match the sample's quality, the buyer must be allowed to inspect and compare, and goods must be free from latent defects that ordinary examination would not reveal.
legal_ingredients: Contract of sale by sample
Bulk shipment must correspond with sample in quality
Mandatory reasonable opportunity to inspect bulk against sample
Freedom from latent unmerchantable defects
17.punishment_or_remedy: Right to reject entire consignment and recover payment with damages.
exceptions_and_limitations: Patent defects that were obvious on simple inspection of sample are not protected.
17.applicability_notes: Vital in wholesale textile, agricultural grain, and manufacturing raw material supply contracts.

46.official_text: (1) Subject to the provisions of this Act and of any law for the time being in force, the unpaid seller of goods, as such, has by implication of law— (a) a lien on the goods for the price while he is in possession of them; (b) in case of the insolvency of the buyer, a right of stopping the goods in transit after he has parted with the possession of them; (c) a right of re-sale as limited by this Act.
46.simplified_explanation: Grants an unpaid commercial seller three strong statutory remedies if the buyer defaults on payment: the right to keep possession of goods under lien, the right to stop goods in transit if buyer is insolvent, and the right to resell the goods.
legal_ingredients: Seller to whom whole of price has not been paid or tendered
Possession of goods retained (lien), or goods in transit with carrier, or right of resale
46.punishment_or_remedy: Lien on goods, stoppage in transit, and right of resale under Section 54.
exceptions_and_limitations: Lien is lost once seller delivers goods to carrier without reserving disposal rights or buyer lawfully obtains possession.
46.applicability_notes: Essential commercial protection for wholesalers and manufacturers against defaulting corporate buyers.

55.official_text: (1) Where under a contract of sale the property in the goods has passed to the buyer and the buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to pay for the goods according to the terms of the contract, the seller may sue him for the price of the goods. (2) Where under a contract of sale the price is payable on a day certain irrespective of delivery and the buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to pay such price, the seller may sue him for the price although the property in the goods has not passed and the goods have not been appropriated to the contract.
55.simplified_explanation: Authorizes a seller to file a civil suit directly for the recovery of the full agreed price (plus interest) when ownership has passed to the buyer and the buyer wrongfully refuses to pay.
legal_ingredients: Property in goods has passed to buyer, or payment due on date certain irrespective of delivery
Buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to pay agreed price
55.punishment_or_remedy: Decree for full contract price plus statutory interest under Interest Act 1978.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to 3-year limitation period under Article 55 of Limitation Act 1963.
55.applicability_notes: Standard statutory basis for recovery of commercial supply invoice arrears.

56.official_text: Where the buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to accept and pay for the goods, the seller may sue him for damages for non-acceptance.
56.simplified_explanation: Gives the seller the right to sue the buyer for damages (market price difference, storage, and transport losses) if the buyer wrongfully cancels an order or refuses to accept delivery.
legal_ingredients: Valid contract of sale
Buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to accept delivery and pay
Seller suffered loss (difference between contract price and market price at date of breach)
56.punishment_or_remedy: Damages representing difference between contract price and market price on date of breach.
exceptions_and_limitations: Seller has a legal duty to mitigate damages by attempting resale in the open market.
56.applicability_notes: Protects manufacturers against sudden client order cancellations after raw materials have been committed.

msmed_act_2006.official_act_name: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006

15.official_section_title: Liability of buyer to make payment
15.official_text: Where any supplier supplies any goods or renders any services to any buyer, the buyer shall make payment therefor on or before the date agreed upon between him and the supplier in writing or, where there is no agreement before the appointed day: Provided that in no case the period agreed upon between the supplier and the buyer in writing shall exceed forty-five days from the day of acceptance or the day of deemed acceptance.
15.simplified_explanation: Strictly mandates that commercial buyers and clients must pay MSME suppliers, freelancers, and small vendors within the agreed time, which can NEVER exceed 45 days under any circumstances.
15.applicability_notes: Primary statutory protection for small vendors, freelance software developers, and MSME contractors against delayed corporate payments.
15.citation: Section 15, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006
15.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
15.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

16.official_section_title: Date from which and rate at which interest is payable
16.official_text: Where any buyer fails to make payment of the amount to the supplier, as required under section 15, the buyer shall, notwithstanding anything contained in any agreement between the buyer and the supplier or in any law for the time being in force, be liable to pay compound interest with monthly rests to the supplier on that amount from the appointed day... at three times of the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank.
16.simplified_explanation: Mandates that buyers who delay payment to MSMEs beyond 45 days are legally liable to pay penal compound interest with monthly rests at THREE TIMES the RBI bank rate.
16.applicability_notes: Statutory interest penalty that overrides any contrary client agreement or contractual waiver.
16.citation: Section 16, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006
16.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
16.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

18.official_section_title: Reference to Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council
18.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any party to a dispute with regard to any amount due under section 17, may make a reference to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council. (2) On receipt of a reference under sub-section (1), the Council shall either itself conduct conciliation in the matter or seek the assistance of any institution or centre.
18.simplified_explanation: Empowers MSME suppliers and registered freelancers to refer payment disputes directly to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council (via MSME Samadhaan portal) for statutory recovery.
18.applicability_notes: Fast-track statutory dispute mechanism allowing registered small vendors to recover dues without prolonged civil court litigation.
18.citation: Section 18, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006
18.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
18.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

8.official_text: (1) A Data Fiduciary shall, irrespective of any agreement to the contrary or for that matter, any failure of a Data Principal to carry out the duties provided under this Act, be responsible for complying with the provisions of this Act... (5) A Data Fiduciary shall protect personal data in its possession or under its control, including in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor, by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach. (6) In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall give the Board and each affected Data Principal, intimation of such breach.
8.simplified_explanation: Imposes strict statutory duty on companies and data fiduciaries to implement robust security safeguards to prevent leaks, and mandates immediate formal notification to citizens in the event of a personal data breach.
8.applicability_notes: Directly applies to corporate data breaches, leaked Aadhaar/PAN records, telemarketing insider data sales, and unauthorized credential exposure.
8.citation: Section 8, Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
8.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
8.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

12.official_text: (1) A Data Principal shall have the right to have readily available means of grievance redressal provided by a Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager in respect of any act or omission of such Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager regarding the performance of its obligations in relation to the personal data of such Data Principal.

25F.official_section_title: Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen
25F.official_text: No workman employed in any industry who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer shall be retrenched by that employer until— (a) the workman has been given one month's notice in writing indicating the reasons for retrenchment and the period of notice has expired, or the workman has been paid in lieu of such notice, wages for the period of the notice; (b) the workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall be equivalent to fifteen days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service or any part thereof in excess of six months; and (c) notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate Government...
25F.simplified_explanation: Statutorily mandates that an employer cannot retrench a workman with 1+ year continuous service without giving 1 month written notice (or wages in lieu) and paying 15 days average pay per completed year of service as retrenchment compensation.
25F.applicability_notes: Statutory protection for industrial workmen, manufacturing workers, and non-managerial staff against arbitrary termination without statutory compensation.
25F.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

33C.official_section_title: Recovery of money due from an employer
33C.official_text: (1) Where any money is due to a workman from an employer under a settlement or an award or under the provisions of Chapter VA or Chapter VB, the workman himself or any other person authorised by him in writing in this behalf... may make an application to the appropriate Government for the recovery of the money due to him... (2) Where any workman is entitled to receive from the employer any money or any benefit which is capable of being computed in terms of money... the question may be decided by such Labour Court as may be specified in this behalf...
33C.simplified_explanation: Provides a statutory mechanism for workers to recover unpaid wages, retrenchment dues, and settlement money from an employer through application to the Labour Court.

25FFA.official_section_title: Sixty days' notice to be given of intention to close down any undertaking
25FFA.official_text: (1) An employer who intends to close down an undertaking shall serve, at least sixty days before the date on which the intended closure is to become effective, a notice, in the prescribed manner, on the appropriate Government stating clearly the reasons for the intended closure of the undertaking...
25FFA.simplified_explanation: Mandates every industrial employer with 50 or more workmen to serve at least 60 days advance written statutory notice on the appropriate Government before closing down any undertaking.
25FFA.applicability_notes: Violated when factories or manufacturing units abruptly shut their gates overnight without statutory government notification or workers' compensation.
25FFA.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

25N.official_section_title: Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen
25N.official_text: (1) No workman employed in any industrial establishment to which this Chapter applies... who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer shall be retrenched by that employer until,— (a) the workman has been given three months' notice in writing indicating the reasons for retrenchment... and (b) the prior permission of the appropriate Government or such authority as may be specified by that Government by notification in the Official Gazette has been obtained on an application made in this behalf.
25N.simplified_explanation: Prohibits retrenchment of workmen in industrial establishments with 100 or more workers without serving 3 months written notice and obtaining prior mandatory permission from the appropriate Government.
25N.applicability_notes: Directly applies to large-scale industrial factory layoffs and mass retrenchments carried out without prior governmental approval.
