2A.official_section_title: Dismissal, etc., of an individual workman to be deemed to be an industrial dispute
2A.official_text: (1) Where any employer discharges, dismisses, retrenches or otherwise terminates the services of an individual workman, any dispute or difference between that workman and his employer connected with, or arising out of, such discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination shall be deemed to be an industrial dispute notwithstanding that no other workman nor any union of workmen is a party to the dispute... (2) The workman may make an application direct to the Labour Court or Tribunal for adjudication of the dispute after the expiry of three months from the date he made the application to the Conciliation Officer.
2A.simplified_explanation: Guarantees that an individual employee who is fired, dismissed, or terminated can file an industrial dispute directly before the Labour Court after 3 months of conciliation, without needing a trade union or other workers to back them.
legal_ingredients: Individual workman discharged, dismissed, retrenched, or terminated
Dispute deemed an industrial dispute by operation of law
Right to apply directly to Labour Court after 3 months of conciliation application
2A.punishment_or_remedy: Reinstatement with full back wages, continuity of service, and compensation.
exceptions_and_limitations: Application must be filed before the Labour Court within three years from the date of discharge or termination.
2A.amendment_status: In force; Section 2A(2) inserted by Act 24 of 2010 granting direct access to Labour Court.
2A.jurisdiction: Central & State Labour Courts / Industrial Tribunals.
2A.applicability_notes: Eliminates the historical barrier where individual non-union employees could not access Labour Courts.

9A.official_text: No employer, who proposes to effect any change in the conditions of service applicable to any workman in respect of any matter specified in the Fourth Schedule, shall effect such change,— (a) without giving to the workmen likely to be affected by such change a notice in the prescribed manner of the nature of the change proposed to be effected; or (b) within twenty-one days of giving such notice.
9A.simplified_explanation: Prohibits employers from unilaterally altering working hours, shift timings, rest intervals, pay allowances, or leave rules without giving affected employees a mandatory 21 days written statutory notice.
legal_ingredients: Proposed change in Fourth Schedule matters (wages, hours, shifts, leave, allowances)
Statutory requirement: mandatory written notice to affected employees
Mandatory 21-day cooling period before change can take effect
9A.punishment_or_remedy: Unilateral change void ab initio; penal action against employer under Section 31.
exceptions_and_limitations: Notice not required where change is effected pursuant to any settlement or award of an Industrial Tribunal.
9A.applicability_notes: Essential defense against sudden employer pay cuts, forced overtime shifts, or arbitrary schedule changes.

10.official_section_title: Reference of disputes to Boards, Courts or Tribunals
10.official_text: (1) Where the appropriate Government is of opinion that any industrial dispute exists or is apprehended, it may at any time, by order in writing— (c) refer the dispute or any matter appearing to be connected with, or relevant to, the dispute... to a Labour Court for adjudication; (d) refer the dispute or any matter appearing to be connected with, or relevant to, the dispute... to a Tribunal for adjudication.
10.simplified_explanation: Statutory mechanism by which the Government or conciliation officer refers an unresolved employer-employee dispute to the Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal for binding judicial adjudication.
legal_ingredients: Existence or apprehension of industrial dispute
Failure of conciliation proceedings (Failure of Conciliation - FOC report)
Formal order of reference by appropriate Government to Labour Court/Tribunal
10.punishment_or_remedy: Binding judicial award enforceable as decree of court; back wages, reinstatement, or financial settlement.
exceptions_and_limitations: Disputes relating to managerial/administrative personnel earning above statutory threshold are excluded from 'workman' definition.
10.applicability_notes: Core dispute resolution path for all collective and referred individual labour disputes in India.

33.official_section_title: Conditions of service, etc., to remain unchanged during pendency of proceedings
33.official_text: (1) During the pendency of any conciliation proceeding before a conciliation officer or a Board or of any proceeding before an arbitrator or a Labour Court or Tribunal or National Tribunal in respect of an industrial dispute, no employer shall— (a) in regard to any matter connected with the dispute, alter to the prejudice of the workmen concerned in such dispute, the conditions of service applicable to them immediately before the commencement of such proceeding; or (b) for any misconduct connected with the dispute, discharge or punish, whether by dismissal or otherwise, any workmen concerned in such dispute, save with the express permission in writing of the authority before which the proceeding is pending.
33.simplified_explanation: Prohibits employers from firing, suspending, transferring, or cutting the pay of employees while a labour dispute is pending before a Conciliation Officer or Labour Court, unless express prior written permission is obtained.
legal_ingredients: Pendency of conciliation or Labour Court proceedings
Alteration of service conditions or dismissal of workman during proceedings
Absence of express prior written permission from conciliation authority/tribunal
33.punishment_or_remedy: Action taken in violation of Section 33 is void ab initio (Jaipur Zila Sahakari Bhoomi Vikas Bank v. Ram Gopal Sharma); complaint under Section 33A.
exceptions_and_limitations: For misconduct not connected with the dispute, employer may discharge on paying one month wages and applying for approval under S. 33(2)(b).
33.jurisdiction: Labour Conciliation Officers and Labour Courts.
33.applicability_notes: Vital shield protecting employees against management retaliation as soon as they approach the Labour Department.

316.official_text: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, or of any legal contract, express or implied, which he has made touching the discharge of such trust, or wilfully suffers any other person so to do, commits criminal breach of trust.
316.simplified_explanation: Criminal breach of trust occurs when someone entrusted with funds, property, or assets dishonestly misappropriates them or refuses to return them in violation of trust or an express agreement. Punishable under Section 316(2) with imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both.
316.applicability_notes: Applies to financial embezzlement, employer non-deposit of PF deductions, fraudulent fund withholding, or unauthorized diversion of client funds.

318.official_section_title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
318.official_text: (1) Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person... commits cheating... (4) Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security... shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
318.simplified_explanation: Cheating involves fraudulently deceiving someone to part with money, property, or sensitive data. Subsection (4) covers serious fraud punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years and fine (replaces former Section 420 IPC).
318.applicability_notes: Core provision for all online financial fraud, UPI scams, fake investment schemes, phishing induced transfers, and fraudulent inducement.
318.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

319.official_text: (1) A person is said to cheat by personation if he cheats by pretending to be some other person, or by knowingly substituting one person for another, or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is. (2) Whoever cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.
319.simplified_explanation: Cheating by personation occurs when a fraudster pretends to be a law enforcement officer, CBI/ED official, bank manager, or someone else to extort or deceive a citizen. Punishable with imprisonment up to 5 years and fine.
319.applicability_notes: Directly applies to digital arrest scams, customer care spoofing, courier customs fraud, and fake government official extortion.

336.simplified_explanation: Creating fake documents, forged signatures, fabricated receipts, or altered electronic certificates with intent to defraud or claim unlawful rights is forgery.
336.applicability_notes: Applies to forged employment contracts, fake bank transfer receipts, forged rent agreements, and fabricated KYC documents.

338.official_section_title: Forgery of valuable security, will, etc.
338.official_text: Whoever forges a document which purports to be a valuable security or a will... shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
338.simplified_explanation: Forging valuable financial securities, cheques, bank guarantees, promissory notes, or property title deeds carries severe punishment up to 10 years imprisonment or life imprisonment and fine.

340.official_section_title: Using as genuine a forged document or electronic record
340.official_text: Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly uses as genuine any document or electronic record which he knows or has reason to believe to be a forged document or electronic record, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had forged such document or electronic record.
340.simplified_explanation: Presenting or utilizing a forged document, screenshot, fake NOC, or tampered electronic record as genuine is punished exactly as if the presenter forged it.

351.official_text: (1) Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do... commits criminal intimidation.
351.simplified_explanation: Threatening injury to a person, their family, property, or reputation (including threats to leak photos, file false cases, or ruin employment) constitutes criminal intimidation.

352.official_text: Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both; and if the threat be to cause death or grievous hurt, or to cause destruction of property... with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

78.official_text: (1) Any man who— (i) follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest... or (ii) monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of stalking. (2) Punished on first conviction with imprisonment up to three years and fine.

79.official_section_title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult modesty of a woman
79.official_text: Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any words, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine.
79.simplified_explanation: Sending sexually explicit messages, lewd remarks, indecent gestures, or intruding into a woman's privacy online or at the workplace is punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.
79.applicability_notes: Applicable to online sexually suggestive harassment, WhatsApp unsolicited obscene media, and verbal workplace misconduct.

281.official_section_title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
281.official_text: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
281.simplified_explanation: Driving or riding a vehicle on a public road in a rash or negligent manner that endangers human life or personal safety is a criminal offence punishable with up to 6 months imprisonment, fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both (replaces Section 279 IPC).
281.applicability_notes: Statutory basis for criminal traffic FIRs involving dangerous driving, stunt riding, or severe negligent maneuvers on public highways.
281.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

125.official_section_title: Act endangering life or personal safety of others
125.official_text: Whoever does any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand five hundred rupees, or with both.
125.simplified_explanation: Any rash or negligent act (such as reckless maneuvering or commercial overloading) that endangers human life or safety without causing grievous injury is punishable with imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs. 2,500.
125.applicability_notes: Applied in traffic collisions, reckless construction diversions, or hazardous vehicle modifications.
125.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

106.official_section_title: Causing death by negligence (including hit and run)
106.official_text: (1) Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine... (2) Whoever causes the death of any person by rash and negligent driving of vehicle not amounting to culpable homicide, and escapes without reporting it to a police officer or a Magistrate soon after the incident, shall be punished with imprisonment... which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
106.simplified_explanation: Causing death through rash or negligent driving is punishable with imprisonment up to 5 years and fine under subsection (1). Under subsection (2), a hit-and-run driver who flees the scene without reporting the incident faces up to 10 years imprisonment and fine.
106.applicability_notes: Pivotal provision for motor accident fatalities and hit-and-run criminal prosecutions.

308.official_text: (1) Whoever intentionally puts any person in fear of any injury to that person, or to any other, and thereby dishonestly induces the person so put in fear to deliver to any person any property, or valuable security or anything signed or sealed which may be converted into a valuable security, commits "extortion". (2) Whoever commits extortion shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

217.official_section_title: Public servant disobeying direction of law with intent to cause injury to any person
217.official_text: Whoever, being a public servant, knowingly disobeys any direction of the law as to the way in which he is to conduct himself as such public servant, intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will, by such disobedience, cause injury to any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
217.simplified_explanation: Penalizes public servants (including police and roadside enforcement officers) who knowingly violate legal procedures, conduct unlawful seizures, or refuse mandatory receipts to harass or harm citizens. Punishable with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine.
217.applicability_notes: Directly applies when enforcement officers arbitrarily impound vehicles or refuse digital receipts to force spot cash payments.
217.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

317.official_text: (1) Property, the possession whereof has been transferred by theft, or by extortion, or by robbery, and property which has been criminally misappropriated or in respect of which criminal breach of trust has been committed, is designated as "stolen property"... (2) Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
317.simplified_explanation: Penalizes anyone who knowingly receives or holds stolen funds or property—including 'cyber mule' bank account holders and UPI account renters who allow fraudulent money to pass through their accounts—with imprisonment up to 3 years, fine, or both.
legal_ingredients: Property transferred through cyber fraud, cheating, theft, or extortion
Dishonest receipt or retention of stolen funds/property
Knowledge or reason to believe funds were illicitly obtained
317.punishment_or_remedy: Imprisonment of either description up to three years, or fine, or both; freezing and attachment of bank account under BNSS Section 107.
exceptions_and_limitations: Innocent account holders whose credentials were hacked without their knowledge are not liable under Section 317 for lack of mens rea.
317.amendment_status: In force; commenced on 1st July 2024 (replacing IPC Section 411).
317.applicability_notes: Primary substantive penal provision applied by cyber police against mule account syndicates and commission agents.

337.official_section_title: Forgery of record of Court or of public register, etc.
337.official_text: Whoever forges a document or an electronic record, purporting to be a record or proceeding of or in a Court of Justice, or a register of birth, baptism, marriage or burial, or a register kept by a public servant in his official capacity, or a certificate or document purporting to be made by a public servant in his official capacity... shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
337.simplified_explanation: Imposes severe punishment—imprisonment up to 7 years and fine—for forging government records, court orders, fake police notices, fake RTO driving licences, or fraudulent official challan slips.
legal_ingredients: Forgery of document or electronic record
Document purports to be court record, public register, police notice, or official certificate
Intent to cause damage or defraud
337.punishment_or_remedy: Imprisonment of either description up to seven years, and fine.
exceptions_and_limitations: Cognizable and non-bailable offence.
337.amendment_status: In force; commenced on 1st July 2024 (replacing IPC Section 466).
337.applicability_notes: Applies directly to cyber extortionists sending fake CBI/Customs warrants and fake traffic challan APK links.

bnss_2023.official_source_name: India Code / Ministry of Home Affairs

173.official_section_title: Information in cognizable cases (Mandatory FIR, Zero FIR, Electronic FIR)
173.official_text: (1) Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing... or if given by electronic communication, shall be taken on record by him on being signed within three days by the person giving it... Provided further that if information is given by electronic communication, it shall be taken on record as an electronic First Information Report (e-FIR)... (2) A copy of the information as recorded under sub-section (1) shall be given forthwith, free of cost, to the informant.
173.simplified_explanation: Police are legally obligated to register an FIR upon receiving information of a cognizable crime. Allows e-FIR for electronic communication and Zero FIR (registration irrespective of territorial jurisdiction). Informants are legally entitled to an immediate free copy of the FIR.
173.applicability_notes: Statutory right of victims to insist on FIR registration for cyber fraud, extortion, theft, or serious traffic accidents.
173.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
173.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

175.official_section_title: Police officer's power to investigate cognizable case
175.official_text: (1) Any officer in charge of a police station may, without the order of a Magistrate, investigate any cognizable case which a Court having jurisdiction over the local area... would have power to inquire into or try. (3) Any person aggrieved by a refusal on the part of an officer in charge of a police station to record the information... may send the substance of such information... to the Superintendent of Police.
175.simplified_explanation: Authorizes police to investigate cognizable crimes immediately without magistrate orders. If an officer refuses to register or investigate, the citizen can appeal directly in writing to the Superintendent of Police (SP) or Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP).
175.applicability_notes: Recourse when local police station refuses to file a cyber fraud or hit-and-run complaint.
175.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
175.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

35.official_section_title: When police may arrest without warrant and notice of appearance
35.official_text: (1) Any police officer may without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person... (3) The police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of a person is not required under the provisions of sub-section (1), issue a notice directing the person against whom a reasonable complaint has been made... to appear before him or at such other place as may be specified in the notice.
35.simplified_explanation: For offences punishable with 7 years imprisonment or less, arrest is not automatic. The police officer must issue a formal written Notice of Appearance directing the citizen to join the inquiry, protecting citizens from arbitrary arrest (replaces Section 41A CrPC).
35.applicability_notes: Protects citizens against unlawful threat of arrest by corrupt officials, recovery agents, or traffic personnel in non-heinous allegations.
35.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
35.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

176.official_section_title: Procedure for investigation and forensic videography
176.official_text: (1) If, from information received or otherwise, an officer in charge of a police station has reason to suspect the commission of an offence... he shall proceed in person, or shall depute one of his subordinate officers... (3) On information of a crime punishable with seven years or more, forensic expert must visit the crime scene and search/seizure shall be recorded through audio-video electronic means.
176.simplified_explanation: Mandates procedural integrity in criminal investigation, including forensic collection and audio-video recording of search and seizures to eliminate evidence planting and police manipulation.
176.applicability_notes: Crucial procedural safeguard in cyber forensic extractions and vehicle accident site documentation.
176.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
176.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

94.official_section_title: Summons to produce document or other thing
94.official_text: (1) Whenever any Court or any officer in charge of a police station considers that the production of any document or other thing is necessary or desirable for the purposes of any investigation, inquiry, trial or other proceeding under this Sanhita by or before such Court or officer, such Court may issue a summons, or such officer a written order, to the person in whose possession or power such document or thing is believed to be, requiring him to attend and produce it, or to produce it, at the time and place stated in the summons or order.
94.simplified_explanation: Empowers investigating police officers and courts to issue formal statutory summons to banks, telecom operators, and crypto exchanges to immediately produce server logs, account statements, CCTV footage, and digital records.
legal_ingredients: Necessity or desirability for investigation, inquiry, or trial
Written summons issued by Court or order by Station House Officer (SHO)
Document, server log, or electronic device in possession of recipient
94.punishment_or_remedy: Failure to comply punishable under BNS Section 223 / IPC Section 175; search warrant under Section 96.
exceptions_and_limitations: Does not affect Sections 123 and 124 of Evidence Act / BSA provisions regarding state secrets.
94.amendment_status: In force; commenced on 1st July 2024 (replacing CrPC Section 91).
94.jurisdiction: Central (Police Officers & Criminal Courts across India).
94.applicability_notes: The primary statutory tool used by Cyber Crime Cells to requisition IP logs, CDRs, and bank transfer trails.

107.official_section_title: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property
107.official_text: (1) Where a police officer making an investigation has reason to believe that any property is derived or obtained, directly or indirectly, as a result of a criminal activity or from the commission of any offence, he may, with the prior approval in writing of the Superintendent of Police or Commissioner of Police, make an application to the Court having jurisdiction to take cognizance of the offence for attachment of such property... (6) Where the Court finds that the property attached is derived or obtained from criminal activity, the Court may pass an order to forfeit the property to the State Government or distribute it to the victim of the offence.
107.simplified_explanation: Authorizes police and Magistrate Courts to formally freeze, attach, and forfeit fraudulent bank accounts and cyber crime proceeds, with a landmark provision empowering the Court to distribute the seized funds directly back to the victim.
legal_ingredients: Property derived or obtained as result of criminal activity or cyber offence
Prior written approval of Superintendent of Police (SP) or Police Commissioner
Court order of attachment and distribution to victim
107.punishment_or_remedy: Judicial attachment and direct refund of frozen money to the victim.
exceptions_and_limitations: Court must issue show-cause notice of 14 days to the affected account holder before final forfeiture.
107.amendment_status: In force; transformative victim-compensation power introduced in BNSS 2023 (replacing CrPC S. 102).
107.applicability_notes: Statutory game-changer for cyber victims; allows Magistrate to release frozen mule account funds directly back to the defrauded citizen.

posh_act_2013.official_act_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
posh_act_2013.official_source_name: India Code / Ministry of Women and Child Development

4.official_text: (1) Every employer of a workplace shall, by an order in writing, constitute a Committee to be known as the 'Internal Committee'... Provided that where the offices or administrative units of the workplace are located at different places or divisional or sub-divisional level, the Internal Committee shall be constituted at all administrative units or offices. (2) The Internal Committee shall consist of Presiding Officer (senior woman employee), at least two members from employees, and one external member from an NGO or familiar with sexual harassment issues; at least one-half of members shall be women.
4.simplified_explanation: Every organization with 10 or more employees is legally required to constitute an Internal Committee (IC) headed by a senior woman employee, with at least 50% women members and an independent external member.
4.applicability_notes: Statutory prerequisite in all commercial establishments, tech firms, factories, and offices.
4.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
4.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

9.official_text: (1) Any aggrieved woman may make, in writing, a complaint of sexual harassment at workplace to the Internal Committee if so constituted, or the Local Committee, within a period of three months from the date of incident and in case of a series of incidents, within a period of three months from the date of last incident: Provided that the Internal Committee... may extend the time limit... not exceeding three months, if it is satisfied that the circumstances were such which prevented the woman from filing a complaint.
9.simplified_explanation: An aggrieved woman can file a formal complaint with the Internal Committee within 3 months of the incident (extendable by an additional 3 months for reasonable grounds). Where the woman is unable to write, the IC must provide all reasonable assistance.
9.applicability_notes: Filing statutory complaints for workplace sexual harassment, hostile work environment, or quid-pro-quo demands.
9.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
9.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

10.official_text: (1) The Internal Committee or, as the case may be, the Local Committee, may, before initiating an inquiry under section 11 and at the request of the aggrieved woman take steps to settle the matter between her and the respondent through conciliation: Provided that no monetary settlement shall be made as a basis of conciliation.
10.simplified_explanation: Before initiating inquiry, the IC may at the aggrieved woman's request attempt informal conciliation. Monetary settlement is strictly prohibited as a basis for conciliation.
10.applicability_notes: Applies where the complainant explicitly desires apology or structural reassignment without formal inquiry.
10.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
10.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

11.official_text: (1) Subject to the provisions of section 10, the Internal Committee... shall, where the respondent is an employee, proceed to make inquiry into the complaint in accordance with the provisions of the service rules applicable... (4) The inquiry under sub-section (1) shall be completed within a period of ninety days.
11.simplified_explanation: The Internal Committee must conduct a fair, impartial inquiry adhering to natural justice, with legal powers of a civil court to summon witnesses and examine documents. The inquiry must be completed within 90 days.
11.applicability_notes: Governs the evidentiary procedure and 90-day time-bound inquiry into workplace harassment.
11.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
11.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

12.official_section_title: Action during pendency of inquiry (Interim Relief)
12.official_text: (1) During the pendency of an inquiry, on a written request made by the aggrieved woman, the Internal Committee... may recommend to the employer to— (a) transfer the aggrieved woman or the respondent to any other workplace; or (b) grant leave to the aggrieved woman up to a period of three months; or (c) grant such other relief to the aggrieved woman as may be prescribed. (2) The leave granted under sub-section (1) shall be in addition to the leave she would be otherwise entitled.
12.simplified_explanation: During inquiry, the woman is legally entitled to interim protections: immediate transfer of the respondent or herself, restraining reporting appraisals, and up to 3 months fully paid leave over and above her regular leave balance.
12.applicability_notes: Statutory right to safe working conditions and protection against retaliation while inquiry is pending.
12.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
12.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

13.official_text: (1) On the completion of an inquiry under this Act, the Internal Committee... shall provide a report of its findings to the employer... within a period of ten days from the date of completion of the inquiry... (3) The employer shall act upon the recommendation within sixty days of its receipt by him.
13.simplified_explanation: IC must deliver its inquiry report within 10 days of completion. If allegations are substantiated, the employer must implement recommended disciplinary action (written apology, withholding promotion, salary deduction for compensation, or termination) within 60 days.
13.applicability_notes: Enforces mandatory employer compliance with IC recommendations within 60 days.
13.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
13.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

26.official_section_title: Penalty for non-compliance with provisions of Act
26.official_text: (1) Where the employer fails to— (a) constitute an Internal Committee under sub-section (1) of section 4; (b) take action under sections 13, 14 and 22... he shall be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees. (2) If any employer, after having been previously convicted of an offence punishable under this Act, commits the same offence, he shall be convicted with twice the punishment... or cancellation of licence or withdrawal of registration.
26.simplified_explanation: Employers who fail to set up an Internal Committee or disregard statutory findings face a fine up to Rs. 50,000. Repeat non-compliance triggers double fines and cancellation of business licenses or government registrations.
26.applicability_notes: Direct legal weapon against management that refuses to address sexual harassment or establish an IC.
26.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
26.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

2_n.official_text: "sexual harassment" includes any one or more of the following unwelcome acts or behaviour (whether directly or by implication) namely:— (i) physical contact and advances; or (ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or (iii) making sexually coloured remarks; or (iv) showing pornography; or (v) any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature.
2_n.simplified_explanation: Defines sexual harassment at the workplace comprehensively: covers unwanted physical touch, sexual advances, demands for sexual favours, sexually coloured remarks, sharing explicit media, and any unwelcome verbal or non-verbal sexual conduct.
legal_ingredients: Unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature
Direct or implied advances, demands, or sexually coloured remarks
Workplace context or work-related interaction
2_n.punishment_or_remedy: Triggers mandatory Internal Committee (IC) inquiry; disciplinary action, wage deduction, or termination of respondent.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subjective perception of victim is primary standard; intention of respondent is secondary.
2_n.jurisdiction: Central (Applies across all private and public workplaces in India).
2_n.applicability_notes: Statutory baseline for determining actionable workplace harassment in corporate, industrial, and remote work environments.
2_n.citation: Section 2(n), Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013

3.official_text: (1) No woman shall be subjected to sexual harassment at any workplace. (2) The following circumstances, among other circumstances, if it occurs, or is present in relation to or connected with any act or behavior of sexual harassment may amount to sexual harassment:— (i) implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment in her employment; or (ii) implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment in her employment; or (iii) implied or explicit threat about her present or future employment status; or (iv) interference with her work or creating an intimidating or offensive or hostile work environment for her; or (v) humiliating treatment likely to affect her health or safety.
3.simplified_explanation: Expressly prohibits hostile work environments, quid pro quo harassment, preferential treatment promises, threats to job security, and humiliating conduct affecting a woman's health or psychological safety at work.
legal_ingredients: Workplace conduct creating hostile or intimidating environment
Implied or explicit promise of promotion or threat of demotion/termination connected to sexual conduct
Humiliating treatment affecting health or psychological safety
3.punishment_or_remedy: Disciplinary action, interim transfer of respondent, paid leave to complainant, and financial compensation.
exceptions_and_limitations: Applies to all workplaces including virtual platforms, off-site client meetings, and office parties.
3.applicability_notes: Prohibits corporate environments that silently tolerate toxicity or retaliate against women speaking up.
3.citation: Section 3, Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013

18.official_text: (1) Any person aggrieved from the recommendations made under sub-section (2) of section 13 or under clause (i) or clause (ii) of sub-section (3) of section 13 or sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of section 14 or section 17 or non-implementation of such recommendations may prefer an appeal to the court or tribunal in accordance with the provisions of the service rules applicable to the said person or where no such service rules exist... to an appellate authority notified under clause (a) of section 2 of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946... (2) The appeal shall be preferred within a period of ninety days of the recommendations.
18.simplified_explanation: Provides a statutory right of appeal within 90 days to a court, tribunal, or appellate authority if the Internal Committee (IC) report is biased, procedural guidelines were flouted, or the employer refuses to implement recommendations.
legal_ingredients: Aggrieved by IC recommendations, finding, or employer non-implementation
Appeal filed within 90 days from date of recommendation
Appellate forum: service tribunal, Labour Court, or notified appellate authority
18.punishment_or_remedy: Appellate authority can set aside flawed IC report, order fresh independent inquiry, or enforce compensation.
exceptions_and_limitations: Appeal must be filed within 90 days.
18.jurisdiction: Central & State (Appellate Authorities and High Courts).
18.applicability_notes: Vital legal remedy when company management influences the Internal Committee to whitewash executive misconduct.
18.citation: Section 18, Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013

19.official_text: Every employer shall— (a) provide a safe working environment at the workplace which shall include safety from the persons coming into contact at the workplace; (b) display at any conspicuous place in the workplace, the penal consequences of sexual harassments; and the order constituting, the Internal Committee; (c) organise workshops and awareness programmes at regular intervals for sensitising the employees... (h) cause to initiate action, under the Indian Penal Code or any other law for the time being in force, against the perpetrator.
19.simplified_explanation: Mandates that employers must provide a safe working environment, display the constitution of the Internal Committee and penal consequences publicly, conduct regular employee sensitization, and assist the victim in filing a police complaint.
legal_ingredients: Employer in private or public sector
Statutory duty to maintain safe working environment, display IC notices, and assist victim in police complaint
Non-compliance punishable under Section 26 with fine up to Rs 50,000 and cancellation of business licence
19.punishment_or_remedy: Penalty up to Rs 50,000 under Section 26; repeated violation leads to cancellation of business licence or registration.
exceptions_and_limitations: Applies to all employers having 10 or more employees.
19.applicability_notes: Employers cannot plead ignorance; failure to constitute IC or conduct sensitization triggers heavy statutory penalties.
19.citation: Section 19, Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013

ni_act_1881.official_source_name: India Code / Ministry of Law and Justice

138.official_section_title: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account
138.official_text: Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person... is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid... such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall... be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both.
138.simplified_explanation: Dishonour of a cheque due to insufficient funds or account closure is a criminal offence. The drawer faces imprisonment up to 2 years, fine up to double the cheque amount, or both.
138.applicability_notes: Statutory foundation for all bounced cheque legal claims, contractor payment dishonours, and debt recoveries.
138.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
138.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

139.official_text: It shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque of the nature referred to in section 138 for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability.
139.simplified_explanation: Law presumes that the recipient holding the bounced cheque received it in discharge of a lawful debt or contractual liability. The legal burden of proof lies entirely on the drawer to disprove this debt.
139.applicability_notes: Crucial statutory presumption that assists payees in recovering bounced cheque amounts.
139.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
139.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

141.official_text: (1) If the person committing an offence under section 138 is a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
141.simplified_explanation: When a corporate entity, firm, or LLP issues a bounced cheque, the company as well as its Managing Directors, signatory directors, and managers in charge of business operations are jointly held criminally liable.
141.applicability_notes: Applies to cheques issued by startup founders, corporate vendors, or registered firms that bounce.
141.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
141.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

142.official_section_title: Cognizance of offences (Statutory timeline and jurisdiction)
142.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure... no court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under section 138 except upon a complaint, in writing, made by the payee... such complaint is made within one month of the date on which the cause of action arises under clause (c) of the proviso to section 138... (2) Offence shall be inquired into and tried only by a court within whose local jurisdiction the branch of the bank where the payee maintains the account is situated.
142.simplified_explanation: Mandates strict statutory timelines: Legal demand notice must be dispatched within 30 days of bank memo. Drawer has 15 days to pay. Complaint must be filed before the Judicial Magistrate within 30 days after the 15-day period expires. Jurisdiction is where the payee holds their bank account.
142.applicability_notes: Strict limitation requirement: failure to serve notice within 30 days or file complaint within 1 month defeats the criminal remedy.
142.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
142.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

143A.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure... the Court trying an offence under section 138 may order the drawer of the cheque to pay interim compensation to the complainant— (a) in a summary trial or a summons case, where he pleads not guilty... (2) The interim compensation under sub-section (1) shall not exceed twenty per cent of the amount of the cheque.
143A.simplified_explanation: The magistrate court can direct the accused drawer to deposit interim compensation up to 20% of the bounced cheque amount in favor of the complainant during the trial within 60 days.
143A.applicability_notes: Provides immediate liquidity relief to complainants during prolonged cheque bounce trials.
143A.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
143A.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

143.official_section_title: Power of Court to try cases summarily
143.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, all offences under this Chapter shall be tried by a Judicial Magistrate of the first class or by a Metropolitan Magistrate and the provisions of sections 262 to 265 (both inclusive) of the said Code shall, as far as may be, apply to such trials... (3) Every trial under this section shall be conducted as expeditiously as possible and an endeavour shall be made to conclude the trial within six months from the date of filing of the complaint.
143.simplified_explanation: Directs that cheque bounce trials under Section 138 must be tried summarily by Magistrates and must be concluded expeditiously within six months from the date of complaint filing.
legal_ingredients: Complaint filed under Section 138 NI Act
Summary trial procedure under CrPC/BNSS
Statutory mandate to conclude trial within six months
143.punishment_or_remedy: Magistrate can pass sentence of imprisonment up to one year and fine exceeding five thousand rupees in summary trial.
exceptions_and_limitations: Magistrate may recall summary procedure and conduct regular summons trial if sentence of over one year may be warranted.
143.amendment_status: In force; inserted by Act 55 of 2002.
143.jurisdiction: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate.
143.applicability_notes: Statutory priority standard enacted to prevent cheque bounce litigation from dragging on for decades.

148.official_section_title: Power of Appellate Court to order deposit
148.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, in an appeal by the drawer against conviction under section 138, the Appellate Court may order the appellant to deposit such sum which shall be a minimum of twenty per cent. of the fine or compensation awarded by the trial Court... (2) The amount referred to in sub-section (1) shall be deposited within sixty days from the date of the order, or within such further period not exceeding thirty days as may be directed by the Court on sufficient cause being shown.
148.simplified_explanation: Empowers Sessions Courts and High Courts hearing an appeal by a convicted cheque defaulter to order mandatory deposit of a minimum of 20% of the compensation awarded by the trial court within 60 days, which can be released to the complainant.
legal_ingredients: Appeal filed by drawer convicted under Section 138
Appellate Court power to order deposit of minimum 20% of fine/compensation
Deposit mandatory within 60 days (extendable by 30 days max)
148.punishment_or_remedy: Mandatory 20% minimum pre-deposit secures interim recovery for complainant; stay vacated on non-deposit.
exceptions_and_limitations: Supreme Court in Surinder Singh Deswal v. Virender Gandhi held that the word 'may' is generally interpreted as mandatory unless exceptional circumstances exist.
148.amendment_status: In force; inserted by Negotiable Instruments (Amendment) Act, 2018.
148.applicability_notes: Stops convicted cheque defaulters from staying sentences without paying any compensation to the victim.

tp_act_1882.official_source_name: India Code / Ministry of Law and Justice

105.official_text: A lease of immoveable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value, to be rendered periodically or on specified occasions to the transferor by the transferee, who accepts the transfer on such terms.
105.simplified_explanation: Defines a tenancy/lease as the legal transfer of the right to occupy and enjoy property for a specified period in exchange for agreed rental consideration.
105.applicability_notes: Statutory foundation for all residential and commercial tenancy agreements and landlord-tenant relationships.
105.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
105.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

106.official_section_title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract (Notice to Quit)
106.official_text: (1) In the absence of a contract or local law or usage to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes shall be deemed to be a lease from year to year, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by six months' notice; and a lease of immovable property for any other purpose shall be deemed to be a lease from month to month, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by fifteen days' notice.
106.simplified_explanation: In the absence of an express contrary clause, residential and commercial leases require a mandatory 15-day written notice to quit expiring with the end of a tenancy month. Landlords cannot unilaterally evict tenants without statutory notice.
106.applicability_notes: Protects tenants from immediate arbitrary eviction and governs legal termination of lease agreements.
106.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
106.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

108.official_section_title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee (Security Deposit refund)
108.official_text: In the absence of a contract or local usage to the contrary, the lessor and the lessee of immovable property, as against one another, respectively, possess the rights and are subject to the liabilities... The lessor is bound to disclose to the lessee any material defect in the property... and is bound to ensure peaceful enjoyment... and on termination the lessee is bound to put the lessor into possession, whereupon the lessor is bound to return the advance/security deposit after lawful deductions.
108.simplified_explanation: Governs statutory rights and obligations: Lessor must disclose latent property defects and guarantee quiet possession. Lessee must pay rent and maintain premises. Upon peaceful handover, the landlord is legally obligated to refund the security deposit, deducting only verified unpaid dues or agreed repairs.
108.applicability_notes: Primary statutory remedy for arbitrary security deposit withholding, unjustified painting deductions, or denial of tenant refund.
108.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
108.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

111.official_text: A lease of immoveable property determines— (a) by efflux of the time limited thereby; (b) where such time is limited conditionally on the happening of some event, by the happening of such event; (c) by the interest of the lessor in the property terminating... (g) by forfeiture; (h) on the expiration of a notice to determine the lease, or to quit.
111.simplified_explanation: Lists the exact legal grounds on which a tenancy terminates, including expiry of agreed duration, surrender, or expiry of a valid statutory notice to quit.
111.applicability_notes: Prevents landlords from declaring unlawful premature termination or illegal lockouts.
111.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
111.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

53A.official_text: Where any person contracts to transfer for consideration any immoveable property by writing signed by him or on his behalf from which the terms necessary to constitute the transfer can be ascertained with reasonable certainty, and the transferee has, in part performance of the contract, taken possession of the property or any part thereof... and the transferee has performed or is willing to perform his part of the contract, then, notwithstanding that where there is an instrument of transfer, that the transfer has not been completed in the manner prescribed therefor by the law for the time being in force, the transferor or any person claiming under him shall be debarred from enforcing against the transferee and persons claiming under him any right in respect of the property of which the transferee has taken or continued in possession, other than a right expressly provided by the terms of the contract.
53A.simplified_explanation: Protects a buyer who paid consideration and took physical possession under a written property agreement: the seller cannot arbitrarily evict the buyer or sell the property to someone else, even if the formal sale deed has not yet been executed.
legal_ingredients: Contract to transfer immovable property for consideration in writing signed by transferor
Transferee has taken physical possession in part performance of contract
Transferee has performed or is ready and willing to perform his part
Statutory debarment of transferor from evicting transferee
53A.punishment_or_remedy: Equitable defense debarring transferor from dispossessing or evicting transferee in possession.
exceptions_and_limitations: Following the 2001 Registration Amendment, Section 53A protection requires the agreement to be registered to defend possession against third parties.
53A.amendment_status: In force; amended by Act 48 of 2001.
53A.applicability_notes: Fundamental doctrine of part performance protecting bona fide purchasers in possession.

54.official_text: "Sale" is a transfer of ownership in exchange for a price paid or promised or part-paid and part-promised. Sale how made.—Such transfer, in the case of tangible immoveable property of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards, or in the case of a reversion or other intangible thing, can be made only by a registered instrument... Contract for sale.—A contract for the sale of immoveable property is a contract that a sale of such property shall take place on terms settled between the parties. It does not, of itself, create any interest in or charge on such property.
54.simplified_explanation: Defines sale of immovable property and establishes that sale of property worth Rs 100 or more can ONLY be legally effected by a registered sale deed. A mere agreement to sell does not transfer title until formal registration.
legal_ingredients: Transfer of ownership in immovable property in exchange for price
Statutory requirement: mandatory registered instrument for property value >= Rs 100
Contract for sale does not itself create proprietary title
54.punishment_or_remedy: Unregistered transfer cannot convey legal title (Suraj Lamp & Industries v. State of Haryana).
exceptions_and_limitations: GPA/SA/Will transfers do not convey title under Suraj Lamp ruling; registered conveyance deed mandatory.
54.applicability_notes: Statutory foundation of Indian property conveyancing law.

107.official_text: A lease of immoveable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding one year or reserving a yearly rent, can be made only by a registered instrument. All other leases of immoveable property may be made either by a registered instrument or by oral agreement accompanied by delivery of possession.
107.simplified_explanation: Mandates that any lease or rental agreement for immovable property exceeding one year (exceeding 11 months) must be executed by a registered instrument, while leases of 11 months or less may be made without registration.
legal_ingredients: Lease of immovable property exceeding one year or reserving yearly rent
Statutory requirement: mandatory registered instrument
Leases for 11 months or less exempt from compulsory central registration
107.punishment_or_remedy: Unregistered lease exceeding one year creates only a month-to-month tenancy terminable by 15-day notice under Section 106.
exceptions_and_limitations: Certain states (e.g. Maharashtra Rent Control Act) mandate registration of all leave and license agreements regardless of duration.
107.applicability_notes: Origin of the ubiquitous '11-month rental agreement' practice in Indian real estate.

limitation_act_1963.official_source_name: India Code / Ministry of Law and Justice

3.official_text: (1) Subject to the provisions contained in sections 4 to 24 (inclusive), every suit instituted, appeal preferred, and application made after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence.
3.simplified_explanation: Courts are legally required to dismiss any suit or recovery application filed after the prescribed statutory limitation period, even if the opposing party does not raise limitation as an objection.
3.applicability_notes: Critical threshold condition for instituting civil breach of contract, debt recovery, and wage recovery claims.
3.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

art_55.official_section_title: Schedule Article 55 - Limitation for breach of contract
art_55.official_text: Description of suit: For compensation for the breach of any contract, express or implied not herein specially provided for. Period of limitation: Three years. Time from which period begins to run: When the contract is broken or (where there are successive breaches) when the breach in respect of which the suit is instituted occurs or (where the breach is continuing) when it ceases.
art_55.simplified_explanation: A civil suit for damages or compensation for breach of contract must be filed within 3 years from the date the contract was broken.
art_55.applicability_notes: Statutory timeline for filing commercial contract damages, vendor defaults, and freelancer payment suits in civil court.
art_55.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
art_55.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

art_7.official_section_title: Schedule Article 7 - Limitation for recovery of wages
art_7.official_text: Description of suit: For wages in the case of any other person. Period of limitation: Three years. Time from which period begins to run: When the wages accrue due.
art_7.simplified_explanation: A civil suit or statutory recovery claim for unpaid wages, salary arrears, or professional remuneration must be filed within 3 years from the date the wages accrued due.
art_7.applicability_notes: Governs the time limit for employees and contractors to recover pending compensation in court.
art_7.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
art_7.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

art_113.official_text: Description of suit: Any suit for which no period of limitation is provided elsewhere in this Schedule. Period of limitation: Three years. Time from which period begins to run: When the right to sue accrues.
art_113.simplified_explanation: For any civil claim, unjust enrichment suit, or security deposit recovery suit where no specific article applies, the limitation period is strictly 3 years from when the cause of action accrued.
art_113.applicability_notes: Applies to security deposit recovery suits, quasi-contractual claims, and restitution of money.
art_113.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
art_113.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.

payment_of_wages_act_1936.official_source_name: India Code / Ministry of Labour and Employment

3.official_text: Every employer shall be responsible for the payment to persons employed by him of all wages required to be paid under this Act.
3.simplified_explanation: Places statutory personal responsibility on the employer, factory manager, or person responsible to the employer to pay all earned wages to employees.
3.applicability_notes: Applies to industrial establishments, commercial offices, and factories.
3.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
3.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

5.official_text: (1) The wages of every person employed upon or in— (a) any railway, factory or industrial or other establishment upon or in which less than one thousand persons are employed, shall be paid before the expiry of the seventh day, (b) any other establishment, shall be paid before the expiry of the tenth day, after the last day of the wage-period... (2) Where the employment of any person is terminated by or on behalf of the employer, the wages earned by him shall be paid before the expiry of the second working day from the day on which his employment is terminated.
5.simplified_explanation: Wages must be paid by the 7th or 10th of each month. When an employee is terminated, all earned wages and settlement amounts must be paid by the employer within 2 working days.
5.applicability_notes: Strict statutory timeline for regular salary payout and 2-day mandatory settlement upon termination.
5.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
5.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

7.official_section_title: Deductions which may be made from wages
7.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding the provisions of any contract, the wages of an employed person shall be paid to him without deductions of any kind except those authorised by or under this Act... (2) Deductions from the wages of an employed person shall be made only in accordance with the provisions of this Act (fines, absence from duty, damage to property entrusted, income-tax, PF contributions, loan recovery).
7.simplified_explanation: An employer is strictly prohibited from making arbitrary salary cuts. Only deductions specifically authorized by statute (PF, tax, absence from duty, or proven entrusted damage) are lawful. All other unilateral deductions are illegal wage theft.
7.applicability_notes: Primary weapon against arbitrary penalty deductions, training bond deductions, and exit laptop withholdings.
7.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
7.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

15.official_section_title: Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
15.official_text: (1) The appropriate Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint a presiding officer of any Labour Court or other officer with experience as a Judge... to be the authority to hear and decide for any specified area all claims arising out of deductions from wages, or delay in payment of the wages... (3) The Authority may direct the refund to the employed person of the amount deducted, or the payment of the delayed wages, together with the payment of such compensation as the authority may think fit, not exceeding ten times the amount deducted.
15.simplified_explanation: Employees can file an application before the Payment of Wages Authority for delayed salary or unlawful deductions. The Authority has the power to order payment of the withheld wages along with compensation up to 10 times the deducted amount.
15.applicability_notes: Statutory forum for recovering withheld salaries and demanding punitive damages from non-compliant employers.
15.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
15.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.

minimum_wages_act_1948.official_source_name: India Code / Ministry of Labour and Employment

12.official_section_title: Payment of minimum rates of wages
12.official_text: (1) Where in respect of any scheduled employment a notification under section 5 is in force, the employer shall pay to every employee engaged in a scheduled employment under him wages at a rate not less than the minimum rate of wages fixed by such notification for that class of employees in that employment without any deductions except as may be authorised within such time and subject to such conditions as may be prescribed.
12.simplified_explanation: Every employer must pay workers wages not less than the statutory minimum wage rates fixed by state or central notifications. Paying below minimum wage is a non-negotiable statutory violation.
12.applicability_notes: Applies to daily wage earners, contract workers, security staff, and entry-level employees across scheduled employments.
12.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
12.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

20.official_text: (1) The appropriate Government may, by notification... appoint an Authority to hear and decide for any specified area all claims arising out of payment of less than the minimum rates of wages... (3) When any application under sub-section (2) is entertained, the Authority shall hear the applicant and the employer... and may direct the payment to the employee of the amount by which the minimum wages payable to him exceed the amount actually paid, together with the payment of such compensation as the Authority may think fit, not exceeding ten times the amount of such excess.
20.simplified_explanation: Employees or registered trade unions can file claims before the Minimum Wages Authority to recover wage deficits, plus statutory compensation up to 10 times the underpaid amount.
20.applicability_notes: Administrative tribunal procedure for unpaid statutory minimum wages.
20.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

22.official_text: Any employer who— (a) pays to any employee less than the minimum rates of wages fixed for that employee's class of work... or (b) contravenes any rule or order made under section 13, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
22.simplified_explanation: Paying less than the prescribed minimum wages is a criminal offence punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months, fine, or both.
22.applicability_notes: Criminal penalty provisions for exploitative wage theft.
22.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
22.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.

18.official_section_title: Prohibition of manufacture and sale of certain drugs and cosmetics
18.official_text: From such date as may be fixed by the State Government by notification in the Official Gazette in this behalf, no person shall himself or by any other person on his behalf— (a) manufacture for sale or for distribution, or sell, or stock or exhibit or offer for sale, or distribute— (i) any drug which is not of a standard quality, or is misbranded, adulterated or spurious; (ii) any cosmetic which is not of a standard quality or is misbranded or spurious...
18.simplified_explanation: Strictly prohibits the manufacture, sale, stock, or distribution of substandard, adulterated, misbranded, expired, or spurious medicines and cosmetics.
18.applicability_notes: Directly applies when pharmacies, medical stores, or online platforms sell expired medicines, fake syrups, or adulterated healthcare products.
18.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

27.official_section_title: Penalty for manufacture, sale, etc., of drugs in contravention of this Chapter
27.official_text: Whoever, himself or by any other person on his behalf, manufactures for sale or for distribution, or sells, or stocks or exhibits or offers for sale or distributes— (a) any drug deemed to be adulterated under section 17A or spurious under section 17B, which when used by any person for or in the diagnosis, treatment, mitigation, or prevention of any disease or disorder is likely to cause his death or is likely to cause such grievous hurt... shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than ten lakh rupees or three times value of the drugs confiscated, whichever is more...
27.simplified_explanation: Imposes severe criminal punishment—imprisonment for 10 years to life and fine of at least ten lakh rupees—for selling or manufacturing spurious or adulterated drugs that cause death or grievous bodily harm.
27.applicability_notes: Applies to criminal prosecution of manufacturers, distributors, and chemists dealing in toxic, counterfeit, or lethal fake pharmaceutical preparations.
27.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

42.official_section_title: Duties of distribution licensees and open access
42.official_text: (5) Every distribution licensee shall, within six months from the appointed date or date of grant of licence, whichever is earlier, establish a forum for redressal of grievances of the consumers in accordance with the guidelines as may be specified by the State Commission. (6) Any consumer, who is aggrieved by non-redressal of his grievances under sub-section (5), may make a representation for the redressal of his grievance to an authority to be known as Ombudsman to be appointed or designated by the State Commission.
42.simplified_explanation: Mandates electricity distribution companies (DISCOMs / BESCOM) to establish a Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF) and Electricity Ombudsman to resolve billing disputes, faulty meters, and arbitrary disconnections.
42.applicability_notes: Statutory forum for domestic and commercial consumers contesting astronomical electricity bills, burnt transformer repair delays, or unmetered tariff overcharging.

56.official_section_title: Disconnection of supply in default of payment
56.official_text: (1) Where any person neglects to pay any charge for electricity or any sum other than a charge for electricity due from him to a licensee or the generating company in respect of supply, transmission or distribution or wheeling of electricity to him, the licensee or the generating company may, after giving not less than fifteen clear days' notice in writing, to such person and without prejudice to his rights to recover such charge or other sum by suit, cut off the supply of electricity... Provided that the supply of electricity shall not be cut off if such person deposits, under protest... an amount equal to that which was arrived at by taking the average of electricity supplied during the preceding six months...
56.simplified_explanation: Prohibits power companies from disconnecting electricity without serving at least 15 clear days' written notice, and prevents disconnection during disputed bill reviews if the consumer pays an average bill under protest.
56.applicability_notes: Protects consumers against abrupt sudden power line disconnection without statutory notice during ongoing billing disputes.
56.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

12.official_text: A complaint in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided may be filed with a District Forum by the consumer to whom such goods are sold or delivered or such service provided or agreed to be provided...
12.simplified_explanation: Governed the procedural filing of consumer complaints before District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forums under the legacy 1986 Act for pre-2019 claims.
