25.official_section_title: Dishonour of electronic funds transfer for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account
25.official_text: (1) Where an electronic funds transfer initiated by a person from an account maintained by him cannot be executed on the ground that the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the transfer instruction or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with a bank, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall, without prejudice to any other provisions of this Act, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the electronic funds transfer, or with both.
25.simplified_explanation: Imposes criminal penal liability (up to 2 years imprisonment and fine up to twice the amount) for dishonour of electronic fund transfers, NACH auto-debits, or e-mandates due to insufficiency of funds.
25.applicability_notes: Statutory counterpart of Section 138 NI Act specifically applying to digital banking, recurring auto-debit payments, and electronic clearing service transactions.
25.citation: Section 25, Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007
25.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.

26.official_text: (1) Where a person committing an offence under this Act is a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company... shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
26.simplified_explanation: Holds directors and key executives of companies personally liable for offences committed under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act.
26.applicability_notes: Applies when corporate entities or fintech payment aggregators commit statutory violations or dishonour payment commitments.

14.official_section_title: Prohibition to use standard mark without licence
14.official_text: (1) No person shall use or exhibit, in respect of any article, process or service, the Standard Mark or any colourable imitation thereof, except under a licence from the Bureau.
14.simplified_explanation: Strictly prohibits using the ISI or BIS Standard Mark or any counterfeit imitation on products without a valid licence issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards.
14.applicability_notes: Directly applies to counterfeit helmets, fake electrical wiring, adulterated packaged drinking water, or duplicate consumer goods bearing unauthorized ISI stamps.

17.official_section_title: Prohibition of manufacture, sale, etc., of goods without standard mark
17.official_text: (1) The Central Government may... direct that any goods, article, process, system or service of any scheduled industry... shall conform to such Indian Standard and direct the use of the Standard Mark under a licence... (2) No person shall manufacture, import, distribute, sell, hire, lease, store or exhibit for sale any such goods without the Standard Mark.
17.simplified_explanation: Prohibits manufacturing, importing, selling, or stocking goods covered under mandatory standard orders without the mandatory BIS certification mark.
17.applicability_notes: Applies to mandatory certified consumer items such as infant food, two-wheeler helmets, cement, LPG cylinders, and electronic adapters.

17.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

29.official_text: (1) Any person who contravenes the provisions of section 14 or section 17 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine which shall not be less than two lakh rupees for the first contravention and not less than five lakh rupees for the second or subsequent contravention, or with both.
29.simplified_explanation: Imposes criminal penalty of up to 2 years imprisonment and a minimum fine of Rs 2,00,000 for manufacturing or selling counterfeit or uncertified goods bearing fake standard marks.
29.applicability_notes: Statutory penal provision for prosecution of rogue manufacturers and merchants peddling hazardous counterfeit items.

7.official_text: Any public servant who— (a) obtains or accepts or attempts to obtain from any person, an undue advantage, with the intention to perform or cause performance of public duty improperly or dishonestly, or to forbear or cause forbearance to perform such duty... shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

7A.official_section_title: Taking undue advantage to influence public servant by corrupt or illegal means
7A.official_text: Whoever accepts or obtains or attempts to obtain from another person for himself or for any other person any undue advantage as a motive or reward to induce a public servant, by corrupt or illegal means or by exercise of his personal influence, to perform or cause performance of a public duty improperly or dishonestly... shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.
7A.simplified_explanation: Penalizes touts, agents, or middlemen who accept or demand money or bribes claiming they will influence a public servant, traffic officer, or RTO authority to waive fines or grant illegal clearances. Punishable with 3 to 7 years imprisonment.
7A.applicability_notes: Applies to middleman networks, touts outside RTOs, or informal bagmen soliciting bribes on behalf of enforcement officials.
7A.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

8.official_section_title: Offence relating to bribing of a public servant
8.official_text: (1) Any person who gives or promises to give an undue advantage to another person or persons, with intention— (i) to induce a public servant to perform improperly a public duty... shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years or with fine or with both. Provided that the provisions of this section shall not apply where a person is compelled to give an undue advantage: Provided further that such person shall report the matter to the law enforcement authority or investigating agency within a period of seven days from the date of giving such undue advantage.
8.simplified_explanation: Penalizes giving bribes, but crucially protects citizens who are coerced or extorted into paying an undue advantage, provided they report the extortion to anti-corruption authorities (Lokayukta/CBI/ACB) within 7 days.
8.applicability_notes: Protects citizens from prosecution when forced to pay spot cash under intimidation or threat of vehicle seizure, provided timely reporting is made.
8.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).

13.official_section_title: Criminal misconduct by a public servant
13.official_text: (1) A public servant is said to commit the offence of criminal misconduct,— (a) if he dishonestly or fraudulently misappropriates or otherwise converts for his own use any property entrusted to him or under his control as a public servant or allows any other person so to do; or (b) if he intentionally enriches himself illicitly during the period of his office. (2) Any public servant who commits criminal misconduct shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than four years but which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine.
13.simplified_explanation: Punishes public servants who engage in habitual bribe collection, pocket unreceipted cash collections, or accumulate illicit assets disproportionate to their lawful income. Punishable with 4 to 10 years imprisonment.

20.official_section_title: Presumption where public servant accepts an undue advantage
20.official_text: Where, in any trial of an offence punishable under section 7 or section 11, it is proved that an accused person has accepted or obtained or attempted to obtain for himself, or for any other person, any undue advantage from any person, it shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that he accepted or obtained or attempted to obtain that undue advantage as a motive or reward such as is mentioned in section 7...

prize_chits_act_1978.official_act_name: The Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978

3.official_section_title: Banning of prize chits and money circulation schemes
3.official_text: No person shall promote or conduct any prize chit or money circulation scheme, or enrol as a member to any such chit or scheme, or keep any office or place for the purpose, or knowingly permit the use of any place for the promotion or conduct of such scheme, or take or receive any money in connection with such scheme.

3.official_section_title: Prohibition of advertisement of certain drugs for treatment of certain diseases and disorders
3.official_text: Subject to the provisions of this Act, no person shall take any part in the publication of any advertisement referring to any drug in terms which suggest or are calculated to lead to the use of that drug for— (a) the procurement of miscarriage in women or prevention of conception... 3.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

4.official_text: Subject to the provisions of this Act, the amount of compensation shall be as follows, namely:— where death results from the injury an amount equal to fifty per cent of the monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor or an amount as notified by the Central Government, whichever is more; where permanent total disablement results from the injury an amount equal to sixty per cent of the monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor...
4.simplified_explanation: Provides statutory mathematical formulas to determine mandatory compensation payable for workplace disablement or fatal casualties based on age and wages.
4.applicability_notes: Specifies mandatory computation of financial awards for injured workmen.
4.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
4.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

4A.official_section_title: Compensation to be paid when due and penalty for default
4A.official_text: (1) Compensation under section 4 shall be paid as soon as it falls due. (2) In cases where the employer does not accept the liability for compensation to the extent claimed, he shall be bound to make provisional payment based on the extent of liability which he accepts... (3) Where any employer is in default in paying the compensation due under this Act within one month from the date it fell due, the Commissioner shall direct that the employer shall, in addition to the amount of the arrears, pay simple interest thereon at the rate of twelve per cent per annum.
4A.simplified_explanation: Mandates that workplace injury compensation must be paid within one month, imposing 12% annual statutory interest and up to 50% penalty for delayed settlement.
4A.applicability_notes: Enforces immediate settlement and penalizes delay in workplace accident payments.
4A.jurisdiction: Central (Applicable across all States and Union Territories of India).
legal_ingredients: Statutory compliance with relevant legal rule.
4A.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory legal remedy, compensation, or penalty as prescribed by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to general statutory exceptions and limitation periods.

57.official_text: Primary evidence means the document itself produced for the inspection of the Court. Explanation 1.—Where a document is executed in several parts, each part is primary evidence of the document... Explanation 5.—Where an electronic or digital record is created or stored, and such storage occurs simultaneously or sequentially in multiple files, each such file is primary evidence.
57.simplified_explanation: Establishes that electronic or digital files stored across computer hard drives, cloud backups, or smartphones constitute primary evidence that courts must accept without secondary certification if the file itself is produced directly.
legal_ingredients: Document or digital record produced directly for inspection of Court
Electronic or digital record created or stored in digital medium
Simultaneous or sequential storage occurring across multiple files or devices
57.punishment_or_remedy: Admissibility as primary proof in criminal trials and civil proceedings.
exceptions_and_limitations: Where the primary digital file is inaccessible or destroyed, secondary electronic evidence may be led subject to Section 63 certificate.
57.amendment_status: In force; commenced on 1st July 2024 via Gazette Notification S.O. 2790(E).
57.jurisdiction: Central (Applies to all courts and judicial proceedings in India).
57.applicability_notes: Essential evidentiary section for all cyber fraud prosecutions and electronic transaction disputes.

61.official_section_title: Admissibility of electronic or digital record
61.official_text: Nothing in this Adhiniyam shall apply to deny the admissibility of an electronic or digital record in evidence on the ground that it is an electronic or digital record and such record shall have the same legal effect, validity and enforceability as other document.
61.simplified_explanation: Provides statutory guarantee that electronic or digital records cannot be rejected by courts merely because they are in electronic format, giving digital evidence identical legal force as paper documents.
legal_ingredients: Record generated or stored in electronic or digital format
Compliance with procedural conditions set out under Section 63
61.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory admissibility of electronic records as legal evidence.
exceptions_and_limitations: Electronic records remain subject to proof of genuineness and integrity of computer source.
61.amendment_status: In force; commenced on 1st July 2024 via Gazette Notification S.O. 2790(E).
61.jurisdiction: Central (Applies across all judicial and quasi-judicial proceedings in India).
61.applicability_notes: Replaces foundational common-law presumptions regarding physical papers, equating digital logs, SMS, and WhatsApp chats to physical letters.

63.official_section_title: Admissibility of electronic records and certificate requirement
63.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Adhiniyam, any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media or cloud or database... shall be deemed to be also a document... (4) In any proceedings where it is desired to give a statement in evidence by virtue of this section, a certificate doing any of the following things, that is to say,— (a) identifying the electronic record containing the statement and describing the manner in which it was produced; (b) giving such particulars of any device involved in the production of that electronic record as may be appropriate for the purpose of showing that the electronic record was produced by a computer... signed by a person in charge of the computer or device, or the management of the relevant activities... shall be evidence of any matter stated in the certificate.
63.simplified_explanation: Mandates that printouts, screenshots, or secondary copies of digital records must be accompanied by an electronic evidence certificate signed by the device custodian or owner to be admissible in court. Replaces former Section 65B of Indian Evidence Act.
legal_ingredients: Information contained in an electronic record produced by a computer or digital device
Device was operating properly during relevant period or malfunction did not affect accuracy
Statutory electronic certificate signed by person in lawful control or management of device
63.punishment_or_remedy: Legal admissibility of secondary electronic evidence; without certificate, secondary digital evidence is inadmissible (Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal).
exceptions_and_limitations: Certificate is not required when the original physical electronic device (original mobile phone/laptop) is produced directly under Section 57.
63.amendment_status: In force; commenced on 1st July 2024 via Gazette Notification S.O. 2790(E).
63.jurisdiction: Central (Applies across all courts in India).
63.applicability_notes: Critical statutory procedural requirement for admitting digital logs, transaction SMS, call records, and WhatsApp chats in cyber fraud prosecutions.

8.official_text: Every employee shall be entitled to be paid by his employer in an accounting year, bonus, in accordance with the provisions of this Act, provided he has worked in the establishment for not less than thirty working days in that year.
8.simplified_explanation: Every employee who has worked in an establishment for at least 30 working days in an accounting year has a statutory entitlement to receive annual bonus from the employer.
legal_ingredients: Employee employed on salary or wage up to statutory ceiling
Worked in establishment for not less than 30 working days in that accounting year
Establishment employs 20 or more persons (or factory under Factories Act)
8.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory right to bonus recovery with interest; recovery through Labour Commissioner under Section 21.
exceptions_and_limitations: Employee must not be disqualified under Section 9 for fraud, theft, or violent misconduct.
8.amendment_status: In force; wage ceiling amended by Act 6 of 2016.
8.jurisdiction: Central (Enforced by Central and State Labour Departments).
8.applicability_notes: Mandatory statutory right of workmen; cannot be contracted out via appointment letters or company policies.

9.official_text: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, an employee shall be disqualified from receiving bonus under this Act, if he is dismissed from service for— (a) fraud; or (b) riotous or violent behaviour while on the premises of the establishment; or (c) theft, misappropriation or sabotage of any property of the establishment.
9.simplified_explanation: An employee loses right to bonus only if formally dismissed after domestic inquiry specifically for fraud, violence on premises, or theft/sabotage. Employer cannot forfeit bonus arbitrarily without formal dismissal on these statutory grounds.
legal_ingredients: Formal order of dismissal from service
Dismissal order expressly based on proved fraud, riotous/violent behaviour, or theft/sabotage
9.punishment_or_remedy: Forfeiture of bonus applies strictly to the accounting year of dismissal.
exceptions_and_limitations: Resignation, ordinary termination, or performance issues do not disqualify an employee from receiving statutory bonus.
9.applicability_notes: Employers often falsely cite resignation to deny bonus; this section strictly limits forfeiture to proved dismissals for grave misconduct.

10.official_text: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, every employer shall be bound to pay to every employee in respect of the accounting year... a minimum bonus which shall be 8.33 per cent. of the salary or wage earned by the employee during the accounting year or one hundred rupees, whichever is higher, whether or not the employer has any allocable surplus in the accounting year.
10.simplified_explanation: Mandates that employers must pay a minimum statutory bonus of 8.33% of wages (or Rs 100), regardless of whether the establishment made a profit or suffered a loss in that accounting year.
legal_ingredients: Covered establishment
Eligible employee who worked 30+ days
Payment mandatory regardless of profit, loss, or allocable surplus
10.punishment_or_remedy: Right to claim 8.33% minimum wage bonus plus interest; penal prosecution of employer under Section 28.
exceptions_and_limitations: New establishments are exempt from paying minimum bonus during first 5 accounting years only if they have not derived any profit.
10.amendment_status: In force; minimum percentage frozen at 8.33%.
10.applicability_notes: Commonly violated when employers claim company suffered losses to deny annual Diwali or financial year-end bonus.

19.official_text: All amounts payable to an employee by way of bonus under this Act shall be paid in cash by his employer— (a) where there is a dispute regarding payment of bonus... within a month from the date on which the award comes into operation; (b) in any other case, within a period of eight months from the close of the accounting year.
19.simplified_explanation: Requires employers to pay all bonus amounts in cash within 8 months from the close of the accounting year (by 30th November for March financial years).
legal_ingredients: Bonus payable under the Act
Payment must be made in cash/bank transfer within 8 months from financial year end
19.punishment_or_remedy: Statutory recovery application before Labour Officer; penal action under Section 28.
exceptions_and_limitations: Appropriate Government may extend the 8-month period on application by employer, but total period cannot exceed 2 years.
19.applicability_notes: Enforces strict deadline on corporate bonus disbursement; employers cannot postpone bonus indefinitely.

28.official_section_title: Penalty for contravention of Act or rules
28.official_text: If any person— (a) contravenes any of the provisions of this Act or any rule made thereunder; or (b) to whom a direction is given or a requisition is made under this Act fails to comply... he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
28.simplified_explanation: Imposes criminal punishment of imprisonment up to 6 months, fine up to Rs 1,000, or both on employers who fail to pay statutory bonus or violate the rules.
legal_ingredients: Willful failure to pay bonus or comply with statutory directions
Complaint filed by or under authority of appropriate Government
28.punishment_or_remedy: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.
exceptions_and_limitations: Cognizance taken only on complaint by or with sanction of Labour Department.
28.applicability_notes: Criminal deterrence against employers withholding statutory employee bonuses.

17.official_section_title: Documents of which registration is compulsory
17.official_text: (1) The following documents shall be registered... (a) instruments of gift of immovable property; (b) other non-testamentary instruments which purport or operate to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish... any right, title or interest... of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards, to or in immovable property; (d) leases of immovable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent.
17.simplified_explanation: Specifies documents that legally must be registered with the Sub-Registrar: property gifts, sales/transfers of immovable property worth Rs 100 or more, and tenancy leases exceeding 11 months (one year or more).
legal_ingredients: Document purporting to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish right/title/interest in immovable property
Value of property rights Rs 100 or upwards, or lease term exceeding one year
17.punishment_or_remedy: Mandatory requirement of law; failure invokes evidentiary bar under Section 49.
exceptions_and_limitations: Residential rental agreements for 11 months or less are not compulsorily registrable under Central Section 17(1)(d), though state stamp laws apply.
17.amendment_status: In force; state amendments in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu require registration of leave and license.
17.applicability_notes: Foundation of all immovable property and tenancy disputes in India; unregistered long-term leases create severe legal infirmities.

49.official_section_title: Effect of non-registration of documents required to be registered
49.official_text: No document required by section 17 or by any provision of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, to be registered shall— (a) affect any immovable property comprised therein, or (b) confer any power to adopt, or (c) be received as evidence of any transaction affecting such property... Provided that an unregistered document affecting immovable property and required by this Act or the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, to be registered may be received as evidence of a contract in a suit for specific performance under Chapter II of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, or as evidence of any collateral transaction not required to be effected by registered instrument.
49.simplified_explanation: An unregistered document that required compulsory registration cannot transfer title or be received as evidence of property transfer in court, but may be admitted to prove a contract in a specific performance suit or for collateral purposes.
legal_ingredients: Document required by Section 17 to be registered
Failure to register with Sub-Registrar
Inadmissibility to affect property or prove transfer
49.punishment_or_remedy: Inadmissibility in evidence; limited exception for specific performance suits or collateral facts.
exceptions_and_limitations: Unregistered agreement to sell can be received as evidence of contract in suit for specific performance under proviso to S. 49.
49.applicability_notes: Crucial statutory barrier in property litigation; protects buyers under specific performance while penalizing unregistered transfers.

3.official_text: (1) No enterprise or association of enterprises or person or association of persons shall enter into any agreement in respect of production, supply, distribution, storage, acquisition or control of goods or provision of services, which causes or is likely to cause an appreciable adverse effect on competition within India. (2) Any agreement entered into in contravention of the provisions contained in sub-section (1) shall be void. (3) Any agreement entered into between enterprises... including cartels, engaged in identical or similar trade of goods or provision of services, which— (a) directly or indirectly determines purchase or sale prices; (b) limits or controls production, supply, markets; (c) shares the market... shall be presumed to have an appreciable adverse effect on competition.
3.simplified_explanation: Declares agreements between businesses that harm fair competition—such as price fixing cartels, bid rigging, artificial market allocation, and forced tie-in sales (e.g. schools forcing books/uniforms from single vendor)—illegal and void.
legal_ingredients: Agreement between enterprises or persons
Appreciable adverse effect on competition (AAEC) in India
Price fixing, market allocation, bid rigging, or tie-in arrangement
3.punishment_or_remedy: Agreement void ab initio; penalty up to 10% of average turnover or 3 times profit for cartel members under Section 27.
exceptions_and_limitations: Reasonable conditions necessary for protecting intellectual property rights (patents, trademarks, copyrights) are exempt under S. 3(5).
3.amendment_status: In force; amended by Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023.
3.jurisdiction: Central (Applies across all commercial enterprises in India).
3.applicability_notes: Directly empowers consumers to challenge collusive price hikes, airline ticket cartels, and school vendor tie-in exploitation.

4.official_text: (1) No enterprise or group shall abuse its dominant position. (2) There shall be an abuse of dominant position under sub-section (1), if an enterprise or a group.— (a) directly or indirectly, imposes unfair or discriminatory— (i) condition in purchase or sale of goods or service; or (ii) price in purchase or sale (including predatory price) of goods or service... (b) limits or restricts— (i) production of goods or provision of services; (c) indulges in practice or practices resulting in denial of market access in any manner.
4.simplified_explanation: Prohibits powerful market leaders and dominant digital platforms from exploiting consumers through unfair prices, predatory pricing below cost to wipe out competition, or blocking market access.
legal_ingredients: Dominant position held by enterprise in relevant geographic and product market
Abusive conduct: unfair conditions, predatory pricing, denial of market access, or leveraging dominance
4.punishment_or_remedy: Cease and desist order, division of dominant enterprise, penalty up to 10% of average turnover under Section 27.
exceptions_and_limitations: Mere possession of dominant market share is not illegal; the statutory violation requires proof of abusive conduct.
4.amendment_status: In force; global turnover penalty standard introduced by Act 9 of 2023.
4.applicability_notes: Primary weapon against Big Tech and monopolistic entities imposing unfair terms on Indian consumers.

19.official_section_title: Inquiry into certain agreements and dominant position
19.official_text: (1) The Commission may inquire into any alleged contravention of the provisions contained in sub-section (1) of section 3 or sub-section (1) of section 4 either on its own motion or on— (a) receipt of any information, in such manner and accompanied by such fee as may be determined by regulations, from any person, consumer or their association or trade association; or (b) a reference made to it by the Central Government or a State Government or a statutory authority.
19.simplified_explanation: Empowers any individual consumer, citizen, trade association, or government body to file an information complaint before the Competition Commission of India (CCI) to investigate cartels or anti-competitive practices.
legal_ingredients: Information petition submitted by consumer, person, or association
Prima facie contravention of Section 3 (anti-competitive agreement) or Section 4 (abuse of dominance)
19.punishment_or_remedy: Director General (DG) investigation; interim relief under Section 33; final penalty and restitution orders under Section 27.
exceptions_and_limitations: CCI will close information at Section 26(2) stage if no prima facie competition concern is disclosed.
19.applicability_notes: Key procedural gateway enabling citizens to trigger antitrust investigations against corporate cartels.

3.official_text: (1) Within six months from the date on which this Act becomes applicable to an industrial establishment, the employer shall submit to the Certifying Officer five copies of the draft standing orders proposed by him for adoption in his industrial establishment. (2) Provision shall be made in such draft for every matter set out in the Schedule which may be applicable to the industrial establishment.
3.simplified_explanation: Mandates employers in industrial establishments with 100 or more workmen to draft and formally certify standing orders defining transparent rules for employment classification, shift work, attendance, and misconduct inquiries.
legal_ingredients: Industrial establishment with 100+ workmen (or state lower threshold)
Submission of draft standing orders covering all Schedule matters within 6 months
3.punishment_or_remedy: Certifying Officer certification; fine up to Rs 5,000 for employer failure to submit draft under Section 13.
exceptions_and_limitations: Establishments with less than the statutory threshold (unless notified by State) are governed by model standing orders.
3.applicability_notes: Statutory safeguard against arbitrary management rules; standing orders have statutory force of contract.

10A.official_text: (1) Where any workman is suspended by the employer pending investigation or inquiry into complaints or charges of misconduct against him, the employer shall pay to such workman a subsistence allowance— (a) at the rate of fifty per centum of the wages which the workman was entitled to immediately preceding the date of such suspension, for the first ninety days of suspension; and (b) at the rate of seventy-five per centum of such wages for the remaining period of suspension if the delay in the completion of disciplinary proceedings against such workman is not directly attributable to the conduct of such workman.
10A.simplified_explanation: Establishes a mandatory statutory right that any employee suspended pending domestic inquiry must be paid subsistence allowance: 50% salary for first 90 days, and 75% thereafter if delay is not caused by the employee.
legal_ingredients: Workman suspended by employer pending inquiry into misconduct
Statutory entitlement to 50% wages for first 90 days of suspension
Rate increases to 75% wages after 90 days if delay is not employee fault
10A.punishment_or_remedy: Recovery of unpaid subsistence allowance with interest; inquiry proceedings vitiated and termination void if subsistence allowance is withheld (Supreme Court in State of Maharashtra v. Chandrabhan).
exceptions_and_limitations: Subsistence allowance is not reduced if the employee obtains an adjournment with valid medical reason.
10A.amendment_status: In force; inserted by Act 18 of 1982.
10A.applicability_notes: High-impact protection against employer starvation tactics during prolonged suspension and disciplinary inquiries.
